World.title: El Gobierno confía en despejar las playas de Ceuta tras desbloquear la Audiencia Nacional el traslado al puerto
World.content:
Migrantes que viven en las chozas de la playa de El Trampolín a la espera del nuevo campamento temporal del muelle de Poniente del puerto de Ceuta, el pasado día 16.

El Ejecutivo presionó al máximo porque una suspensión habría arruinado su plan de salida. La Moncloa cree que el SUP eligió el momento más dañino

Durante unas horas del miércoles, el Gobierno entró en combustión. La decisión de la Audiencia Nacional paralizaba el traslado de 1.700 inmigrantes al puerto de Ceuta en el momento crítico. No se había anunciado públicamente, para evitar altercados, pero la idea era moverlos desde las playas de El Trampolín y Benítez hasta el puerto a primera hora de este jueves.

El Gobierno se indignó con la Audiencia Nacional pero sobre todo con el Sindicato Unificado de Policía (SUP), que había reclamado esta medida cautelar justo el día anterior del traslado que la policía conocía, porque se había preparado con ellos para que todo saliera bien. “Es imposible que sea casual, lo sabían e intentaron boicotearnos”, señala un miembro del Gobierno. En La Moncloa hubo una especie de gabinete de crisis, como casi siempre, pero no formal, sino como ronda de llamadas para ver opciones y tomar decisiones.

Con el propio presidente encima de todos los movimientos y tres ministros muy directamente implicados, Ángel Víctor Torres, Óscar Puente y Elma Saiz, se decidió salir a la ofensiva. El Gobierno transmitía oficialmente un mensaje de “perplejidad” y exigía una solución rápida con una idea: “Ceuta no puede esperar”.

Aun así, a esas horas de la noche, las 21.30, y después del shock inicial, el Ejecutivo ya empezaba a manejar la idea de que la Audiencia Nacional decidiera este mismo jueves y lo hiciera a su favor. Pero no tenía garantías, así que decidió presionar con toda la fuerza. Ahora en La Moncloa no son capaces de saber si los jueces reaccionaron a su presión o habrían tomado esta decisión de todos modos, pero creen que valió la pena asegurarse.

En la mañana del jueves, tanto Puente como Óscar López comparecieron en varios medios para mantener esa presión, pero con un tono comedido para el que suele ser habitual en ambos, conscientes de la que la decisión podía ser positiva y no era conveniente subir la temperatura más de lo necesario.

El ministerio de Puente había enviado en la noche del miércoles dos decenas de documentos extensos a la Audiencia Nacional para demostrar que todo estaba en regla y con las prevenciones de seguridad tomadas y todos los informes reglamentarios a favor de llevar a los inmigrantes al puerto. “Nos hablan de seguridad, pero ¿qué es más seguro, que estén en el puerto en una zona acondicionada con baños y duchas y rodeados de seguridad privada y policías o que estén en unas chabolas improvisadas en la playa y haciendo sus necesidades donde pueden?”, insistían esa mañana desde el Gobierno.

En ese momento el Ejecutivo trabajaba con la confianza en una resolución positiva, porque no tenían un plan b. Sin el puerto, toda su estrategia para devolver a Ceuta a una cierta normalidad, sacando a 1.700 inmigrantes de las playas y desmantelando sus campamentos, se iba al traste. “Nos piden que hagamos magia, no sé si la gente es consciente de de las dimensiones de Ceuta, hay muy pocas opciones”, sentenciaba Puente en TVE.

Hubo cierto nerviosismo cuando por la mañana los jueces aún no habían descargado la documentación enviada por Transportes y se movía en sectores judiciales la idea de que faltaban papeles. No era así. En cuanto se pusieron a estudiarlos, los jueces levantaron rápidamente el bloqueo y los trabajos, que ya estaban ultimándose el miércoles cuando se paralizaron, se reanudaron enseguida.

Con esta apertura de la ubicación del puerto, que el Gobierno ha buscado desde el principio porque era sencilla, rápida, grande y alejada de las casas de los ceutíes, los técnicos que llevan semanas trabajando sobre el terreno confían en dar un salto muy importante para intentar despejar las playas y cambiar la imagen de hacinamiento que han trasladado las televisiones en los últimos 45 días.

En realidad el Gobierno ya logró una vez despejar la playa de El Trampolín con otro traslado, pero se volvió a llenar enseguida con inmigrantes que bajaron del monte. Esta vez podría volver a pasar, porque aún quedan más de 1.700 personas en las calles y en el monte, pero cada vez son menos y ya se está trabajando en otra ubicación para los que queden, que ahora serán más fáciles de contar.

Además, según diversas fuentes del Gobierno, sigue el lento goteo de inmigrantes que se rinden y se vuelven voluntariamente a Marruecos, ya más de 5.500 desde el 10 de agosto, y en los últimos días con algún pico de 100 diarios. El Gobierno insiste en lanzar el mensaje de que prácticamente ningún marroquí podrá acceder al asilo y por tanto su destino es ser devueltos, con la esperanza de que entiendan que es mejor volver voluntariamente. Pero la gran mayoría siguen quedándose a la espera de acontecimientos.

La crisis no está resuelta, ni mucho menos, pero el hito del puerto es fundamental para completar el plan del Gobierno de tener más de 6.000 personas albergadas y así acelerar el proceso de devolución de la enorme mayoría. Con la otra ubicación que se está trabajando entre varias opciones podría ya rematarse la operación, aunque el Ejecutivo sigue sin saber realmente cuántos son.

Las últimas cifras que ha dado, entre albergados, retornados voluntariamente y personas aún por las calles, supera las 12.000 personas que se quedaron después del salto de julio, el número que inicialmente calculó la ciudad de Ceuta y que el Gobierno negaba.

El número de comidas que se reparten en las calles ya no vale para hacer una estimación porque sigue siendo casi siempre el mismo a pesar de que hay 4.300 personas acogidas que comen en sus instalaciones, lo que hace pensar que algunos inmigrantes que ya estaban en Ceuta antes del 30 de julio están acudiendo a comer y eso altera todo el cálculo.

La crisis ha hecho aflorar a muchas personas que malvivían en la ciudad y ahora han entrado en el bloque de los acogidos. Y no es fácil contar a las personas que duermen escondidas en el monte. El Gobierno tiene previsto llegar si fuera necesario hasta a 10.000 plazas de acogida, pero todo con la idea de devolver a la enorme mayoría.

Mientras, el Gobierno también presiona a Ceuta para que acepte el envío de menores a la Península, sobre todo las 500 niñas más vulnerables, algunas de solo 10 años, pero ahí está abierta una guerra clara con la dirección del PP, radicalmente en contra de sacar un solo menor al resto de España.

El Ejecutivo aún está sentado sobre el enorme barril de pólvora en el que se ha convertido la crisis de Ceuta, pero después de la primera buena noticia judicial en mucho tiempo, la euforia era muy clara en La Moncloa y una nota oficial celebró “la rapidez” de la Audiencia Nacional.

El Gobierno sostiene que ahora viene el trabajo más difícil y más discreto: lograr la velocidad de crucero en la tramitación de expedientes de menores y de adultos para empezar a devolver a inmigrantes a una velocidad constante y poder ver algo de luz en una crisis que ha destruido la imagen de un Gobierno que se había acostumbrado a todo tipo de situaciones extremas y lograba salir airoso de todas ellas, pero esta vez no midió bien la dimensión del problema y tardó mucho más de lo razonable en empezar a enfocarlo. Ahora cree que empieza a tenerlo controlado, pero puede haber aún muchas sorpresas.

World.title: La estafa del falso empleado de banca
World.content:
Recibir un SMS que alerta sobre un movimiento sospechoso en nuestra cuenta bancaria puede evitar que seamos víctima de un robo, excepto si no ha sido el banco quien realmente lo ha emitido

En la estafa del falso empleado de banca el delincuente primero envía un mensaje con una alerta sobre un movimiento sospechoso en la cuenta y facilita un enlace o un número de teléfono al que llamar. Ya en la conversación, intenta convencer a la víctima de que su dinero está en peligro para que autorice operaciones que resultarán fraudulentas

En 2025, Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad (INCIBE) registró 25.133 casos de phishing. Durante los dos últimos años, tanto la Policía Nacional como la Guardia Civil y el Banco de España han emitido alertas sobre el aumento de las llamadas de falsos empleados bancarios.

TÉCNICAS DE MANIPULACIÓN

Autoridad Suplantan a profesionales pertenecientes a bancos a los que la víctima concede poder y confianza Urgencia Crean la sensación de que hay poco tiempo para actuar, lo que evita que la víctima reflexione o consulte con alguien Sobrecarga de información técnica Emplean jerga bancaria para intimidar y hacer creer que dominan una situación compleja Aumento gradual de las peticiones Incluye a la víctima en grupos de aplicaciones de mensajería para hacerle creer que mucha gente ya está ganando dinero

CIBEREXPERTO NOMBRE Jordi Sánchez CARGO Experto en fraude de CaixaBank “Durante la llamada, el estafador te hace creer que te está guiando para solucionar tu problema, pero en realidad, está intentando que tu hagas exactamente lo que necesita, emitir operaciones bancarias, descargar aplicaciones o facilitar información, como códigos o datos de tarjetas” Play / Pause CÓMO EVITAR LA ESTAFA DEL FALSO EMPLEADO DE BANCA 1 Sospechar de mensajes inesperados. No clicar en ningún enlace que aparezca en el mensaje ni llamar al número que ofrecen. Ante la duda, siempre se debe llamar a los números oficiales del banco 2 Desconfiar de la urgencia y de las amenazas.Mensajes como “Su cuenta será bloqueada” buscan que se actúe sin pensar 3 No compartir claves ni códigos de verificación. El banco nunca solicitará contraseñas u otros códigos de seguridad 4 No descargar archivos ni instalar aplicaciones. Los estafadores pueden pedir que se descarguen programas que en realidad les están dando acceso al teléfono de la víctima

Una estafa que ha evolucionado. Este fraude comenzó como un SMS y una llamada, pero hoy se dan variantes como la que busca robar información de las tarjetas bancarias mediante el uso de la tecnología NFC del teléfono móvil. Este sistema de comunicación inalámbrica permite compartir información entre otros, tarjetas y móviles, y realizar pagos sin contacto. Los estafadores solicitan a la víctima que se descargue una aplicación maliciosa y que acerque la tarjeta al smartphone. Así, sus datos son enviados a otro teléfono de los atacantes, donde crearán una tarjeta de forma virtual con la que intentar sacar dinero o comprar en comercios.

El teléfono puede parecer auténtico. Los estafadores pueden hacer que en la pantalla del móvil de la víctima figure el mismo número que utiliza el banco para atender a sus clientes o que el SMS aparezca en el mismo hilo que las comunicaciones legítimas mediante una técnica que se conoce como spoofing (que significa suplantación).

Conocen datos personales de su víctima. En muchos casos, disponen de información de su objetivo, como el banco del que es cliente, parte del DNI o la dirección de correo electrónico.

Si ya se ha caído en la estafa. Se debe poner en conocimiento del banco de inmediato para que se puedan adoptar las medidas operativas oportunas. También es muy importante guardar las evidencias, como capturas de pantalla, SMS, correos y registro de llamadas. Presentar una denuncia ante la Policía Nacional o la Guardia Civil.

OTROS CASOS DEL FALSO EMPLEADO DE BANCA

Cada semana aparecen noticias con nuevas maneras de embaucar a ciudadanos con una estafa de este tipo:

World.title: Firmé las arras de un piso en junio y ahora el vendedor me dice que hay una derrama de 13.000 euros. ¿A quién corresponde pagarla?
World.content:
Los lectores envían sus preguntas al consultorio de vivienda de EL PAÍS en colaboración con Legálitas

Pregunta. A principios de junio firmé un contrato de arras con un plazo de tres meses para escriturar la compra de la vivienda. A finales de junio la junta de la comunidad aprobó una derrama de 13.000 euros por el arreglo del portal y el ascensor. Todavía no he firmado la compraventa y ahora el vendedor me indica que debo hacerme cargo de dichos gastos. ¿A quién corresponde el pago? Jesús María G.

Respuesta. El pago de una derrama corresponde a quien ostente la condición de propietario en el momento en que se exijan cada una de sus cuotas, conforme a lo dispuesto en el artículo 17.11 de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal.

En consecuencia, las cuotas vencidas antes de la firma de la escritura deberán ser abonadas por el vendedor, ya que era el propietario cuando dichas cantidades eran exigibles. Por el contrario, las cuotas cuyo vencimiento se produzca con posterioridad a la firma corresponderán al comprador, al haber adquirido la titularidad de la vivienda, aunque la derrama hubiera sido aprobada antes de la compraventa.

Por último, las derramas que se aprueben una vez formalizada la venta serán asumidas íntegramente por el comprador.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: 24 horas en Ayamonte, la ciudad de Huelva donde vivir uno de los mejores atardeceres de Europa
World.content:
Esta localidad onubense se define por su luz y por su condición fronteriza con Portugal. Hay que visitar su parte alta y la baja, a pie del río Guadiana, y aprovechar el viaje para ir al cercano paraje natural Marismas de Isla Cristina

Ayamonte es una localidad onubense que se define por su condición fronteriza. Su localización geográfica, en la desembocadura del Guadiana, es un punto estratégico en el que estuvieron fenicios, romanos, musulmanes y cristianos y en el que confluyen el mencionado río, el océano Atlántico, marismas, esteros, dunas y dos culturas: la local y la vecina portuguesa. En la orilla de enfrente, se encuentran los pueblos lusos de Vila Real de Santo António y Castro Marim. Las costumbres de unos y otros se filtran en ambas orillas de manera natural. Son humedades enriquecedoras, como ese fado del cantante Carlos Cano titulado María la portuguesa, que narra el trágico incidente de contrabando y amoríos que le costó la vida a un ayamontino en los años ochenta.

Esa posición geográfica aúna valor estratégico y estético. Localización que hizo que Ayamonte, desde el siglo XVI, tuviera un vínculo especial con la navegación, el comercio marítimo y la pesca del atún y de la sardina, actividades que hicieron que la localidad se desarrollara económica y socialmente. En el siglo XIX, tras el tsunami provocado por el terremoto de Lisboa de 1755 y que tanto afectó a Ayamonte, fue el turno de la industria conservera y salazonera. En 1991, se inauguró el Puente Internacional del Guadiana, lo que supuso un gran hito en la relación con Portugal, en la movilidad y en la economía.

Más información Cinco ciudades en España para comer muy bien más allá de Madrid y Barcelona

A su patrimonio histórico y arquitectónico se ha sumado el de la luz. El proyecto europeo Atlantic Sunset ha situado a Ayamonte entre los lugares del arco atlántico donde el sol se pone más tarde —los estudios científicos del proyecto lo han identificado como el lugar donde se produce el último atardecer de la España peninsular entre los meses de octubre y febrero—. Un espectáculo natural que suma otro motivo más por el que merece la pena el periplo hasta aquí. Por carretera se llega desde las ciudades de Huelva, Sevilla y Faro, en Portugal, donde se encuentra el aeropuerto más próximo a Ayamonte y principal puerta de entrada de muchos de los turistas extranjeros que se ven paseando por las calles y las plazas del Rosario, de La Laguna y de La Ribera. En estos escenarios tiene lugar en el mes de agosto Un paseo por el Arte, evento que tiene el fin de mostrar en la calle las obras pictóricas, escultóricas y fotográficas de cientos de artistas locales o con alguna vinculación con la ciudad.

La plaza de la Laguna, en Ayamonte. Vibrant Pictures (Alamy / cordon Press)

10.00 Una habitación con vistas

Si la de Virginia Woolf era una habitación propia, las del Parador Nacional de Ayamonte lo son con vistas; al Guadiana, al Puente Internacional que lo cruza y a la ciudad. Aquí antes hubo un castillo de origen romano, reedificado por los musulmanes después y finalmente ocupado por los cristianos.

Desde lo alto de la colina se divisa el río, Portugal y Ayamonte, que está a sus pies. El pueblo tiene una zona plana, a orillas del Guadiana, y otra alta, donde está el parador. Aia, en árabe, significa zona elevada. Cuando llegaron los cristianos, se encontraron un pueblo que se llamaba Aia y ellos le añadieron el sufijo “monte”. La parte más baja del pueblo se encuentra a unos tres metros sobre el nivel del mar, en las zonas cercanas al estuario; la parte más elevada es la del parador, a 63 metros de altura.

11.00 Antes y después del terremoto

A mediados del siglo XIII, Ayamonte pasó de manos portuguesas a las castellanas. A partir de ese momento, creció al amparo de la familia Guzmán y se vertebró en torno a dos partes: La Villa, la parte alta, donde se concentraban los edificios administrativos y religiosos, y La Ribera, la parte baja, donde se concentraba la vida marítima y comercial.

La Villa está llena de calles estrechas, miradores, fachadas tradicionales, balcones floridos y pequeños rincones con encanto. En este barrio se encuentran templos como El Salvador, San Francisco y San Sebastián, además de antiguos palacios y casas señoriales. Uno de los edificios más emblemáticos es el antiguo Palacio de los Marqueses, junto al “Patio de la Jabonería”.

La iglesia de El Salvador, en la localidad onubense. Felipe Rodriguez (Alamy / cordon Press)

En La Ribera están las casas blancas, el paseo fluvial y el ambiente que evoca su origen marinero. Destacan el Centro Cultural Casa Grande Manuel Rivero “El Pintado”, el Ayuntamiento, las plazas de la Laguna y de La Ribera, conventos como el de las Hermanas de Santa Clara y las iglesias de San Francisco, La Merced y Las Angustias. La Casa Grande es la única casa que se conserva anterior al terremoto de Lisboa de 1775. Seísmo que derivó en un tsunami que afectó gravemente a Ayamonte y otras localidades de Huelva, como Isla Cristina. Destruyó muchos edificios y hubo que reconstruir gran parte de su casco urbano. Las fachadas que hoy se ven datan de aquella época.

La plaza de La Laguna —aquí antes había una— es el corazón histórico y social de la ciudad. En ella hay una la réplica de La pesca del atún en Ayamonte, obra de Joaquín Sorolla integrada en la colección Visión de España que la Hispanic Society de Nueva York encargó al pintor. La plaza de La Ribera la diseñó el arquitecto José Granados, inspirada en las obras de Aníbal González, arquitecto sevillano que hizo la plaza de España. En la misma hay cerámica y ladrillo mudéjar forjado en las farolas, los bancos...

14.00 Geografía en el plato

Puesto de mercado y marisco en el mercado central de Ayamonte. Marcos del Mazo (Alamy / cordon Press)

La gastronomía, como el turismo y la pesca, son algunos de los sectores que forman parte de la economía azul, esa que se nutre de los recursos marinos de manera responsable, generando un crecimiento económico y empleo al tiempo que preserva la salud de los ecosistemas acuáticos de la zona. El abanico de delicias que se pueden degustar incluye la gamba blanca de Huelva, el choco, el atún, la sardina, la caballa, el arroz marinero y la mojama, el jamón del mar.

Estas delicias se preparan desde hace 60 años en el Restaurante Casa Luciano. El negocio hoy lo lleva el hijo del marinero que lo abrió, Luciano Ramos. El menú depende de lo que se coja en el día. En la carta, unos días hay y otros no, morro de atún, gambas a la plancha, cazón seco con tomate, cocido de garbanzos con rape, etcétera. Mucha de esa materia prima viene de Isla Cristina, donde se encuentra la principal lonja de Andalucía y la segunda más importante de España, después de la de Vigo. Cerca de la misma se puede comer en el Bar Marinero y en Doña Lola, a orillas de la ría Carreras.

17.00 Parajes naturales

“Un lugar con tanta riqueza ecológica, como Ayamonte y sus alrededores, tiene un gran potencial como destino de viaje responsable”, sentencia Margarita Arjona, directora de Healing Planet, consultora de turismo sostenible. Alrededor de Ayamonte hay dunas y las marismas del Guadiana y el paraje natural Marismas de Isla Cristina, bañado por la ría Carreras, donde se encuentran Las Salinas del Alemán. Es una explotación artesanal, entre esteros y caños, que tuvo como primer propietario a un espía germano que envió el gobierno nazi en 1939 a la zona, Hans Burghard (o Juanito el alemán, para los lugareños), y que en la década de los ochenta se puso al frente de las mismas Manuel Gómez, al que le siguieron su hija (Manuela) y sus nietas (Estefanía y Sabina).

El paraje natural Marismas de Isla Cristina. Sonia Bonet (Alamy / cordon Press)

Además de esta sal por aquí hay salicornia o espárrago de mar, una planta que nace en las marismas y que el proyecto Marshfood produce de manera pionera. Cocineros como Ángel León, Martín Berasategui y Quique Dacosta la han usado.

18.30 La luz como fuente de orgullo

Si en Ayamonte el Guadiana es frontera, la luz es un orgullo. El pasado mes de enero esta localidad acogió una jornada divulgativa en el marco del proyecto europeo Atlantic Sunset que sitúa al municipio onubense entre los enclaves del arco atlántico donde el sol se pone más tarde. Es decir, es uno de los mejores escenarios europeos para ver el atardecer. Algo que se puede ver en tierra firme o a bordo de una embarcación, ya sea la que hace una travesía por el Guadiana o la que lo cruza con destino la orilla portuguesa.

El Puente Internacional del Guadiana, que conecta Ayamonete con la localidad de Castromarín, en el distrito de Faro (Portugal), al atardecer. juampiter (GETTY IMAGES)

20.30 Una cena de sabores allende los mares

Después de la navegación, se puede cenar en el LPA The culinary bar, un restaurante inesperado en Ayamonte. Su cocina fusiona la tradición con la creatividad con posos de los viajes realizados por su cocinero italiano, Fabio Zerbo. El risotto de boletus con trufa, un curri tikka masala con pan naan casero o un arroz de corvina y maracuyá son algunos de los platos de esta casa que se ha convertido en un patrimonio más de la ciudad.

World.title: Jetten refuses to pick a side as opposition warns of drama
World.content:
Prime minister Rob Jetten has declined to say whether his minority coalition will seek support from the left or right to pass its first budget, telling MPs on the second day of debates that making that choice now would be “short-changing the country”.

Instead of committing one way or the other, Jetten said the cabinet would send invitations on Thursday evening to seven opposition parties – Pro, JA21, ChristenUnie, SGP, BBB, Volt and 50PLUS – for a new round of talks on support for the current budget and tax plan.

But the two parties whose votes matter most, which are pulling left and right, have said they see little point in such talks. Opposition party Pro leader Jesse Klaver said more discussions would be a repeat of the ones that collapsed in the summer.

Far-right JA21 leader Joost Eerdmans said the cabinet had to choose. “Broad isn’t going to work,” he told Jetten. “Which way are you going?”

Jetten admitted the cabinet had underestimated how much time it needed in August to work opposition demands into the budget, and said it wanted to keep talking in the coming weeks. He again said a broad agreement was his preference, but did not rule out seeking support for individual budgets if needed.

“A drama for the Netherlands”

Klaver said the coalition is “divided to the bone”, and told Jetten “lock yourself in a room,” because “if you don’t make the choice, it will grind to a halt and this autumn will be a drama for the Netherlands.”

ChristenUnie leader Mirjam Bikker said it was “hard for us to talk” to a cabinet that could not agree with itself.

On the first day of the debates yesterday, Eerdmans said a total deal with the cabinet was no longer realistic and JA21 would judge each departmental budget separately, ruling out support for the climate budget and probably the asylum budget so long as the spreading law for asylum seekers remains in force.

Klaver responded that Pro would withhold support from every budget if the cabinet struck separate deals with JA21. The coalition of D66, VVD and CDA has 66 of the 150 seats in parliament and needs 16 extra votes in the senate.

Siding with Pro would give it the easiest chance of a majority, but the right-wing VVD does not want to concede to them on many issues.

Stabs in the back

PVV leader Geert Wilders opened the day by confronting Jetten with an article in the newspaper AD, in which unnamed ministers criticised the prime minister for failing to take charge, one saying the only direction he took was the visual direction””, managing the image.

Wilders said Jetten’s colleagues had “stuck three daggers in your back” and asked what he thought of not being trusted by his own party.

Jetten said he was proud of his team and “we are making the best of it”.

Tax plans

In mid-November parliament will vote on the tax plan. Pro and ChristenUnie have both said they will not back it as it stands, because the burden falls largely on people in work, and Eerdmans said there is no way the plan can satisfy both JA21 and Pro at the same time.

The Council of State, the government’s main advisory body, said this week that €5.8 billion of the €6 billion in tax rises planned for 2027 would be paid by workers, while the burden on companies and wealth falls slightly. A decision on the tax on savings and investments, known as Box 3, has been postponed until next year.

Jetten said the cabinet would spend an extra €10 billion on infrastructure in the coming years and told Pro that the nitrogen plans would not be watered down, though “improvements” were possible provided they delivered the same reduction in emissions.

MPs will vote on motions, including a motion of no confidence tabled by Wilders, at the end of the debate on Thursday night.

The Dutch public health institute RIVM has announced a fourth death from West Nile virus in the country, after a patient contracted the disease from a blood transfusion.

The authorities do not yet know whether the person, who was already ill, died directly from the virus.

The total number of West Nile cases is now at 28, with ten new patients reported to RIVM in the last week.

Most were infected by mosquitoes. West Nile virus is harmless to the majority of people. Around 20% of those infected develop mild flu-like symptoms.

The elderly and people with health vulnerabilities have the highest risk of death.

The RIVM also reported that since September 10, there have been 30 reports of horses infected with West Nile virus, bringing the total so far this year to 88.

Around 100 cases have also been found in birds.

World.title: FvD refuses to remove racist podcast episode amid outcry
World.content:
An English language podcast broadcast aired by the far-right FvD party’s international arm, Forum & Friends, has sparked an outcry after guests described African people as “pack animals”, discussed racial IQ theories and described Black people as genetically inferior.

The podcast is a weekly show which, like other party operations, is funded through the interior ministry’s subsidy for political parties.

The August 26 episode was hosted by John Laughland, a British party staffer who has run FvD International since 2022 and is a mentor to party founder Thierry Baudet.

Laughland’s guest was British author Simon Elmer, who had posted a series of messages on X about Jason Arday, a Black Cambridge professor who took his own life earlier this year following plagiarism accusations.

Elmer went on to describe the “genetically determined culture and mentality of African people” and said their only use was “to destroy us and breed us out of existence”. He called people from 10 African countries “feeble-minded”. Laughland nodded along and said at the end that it was “hard to disagree” with the analysis.

“Outlandish”

FvD parliamentary leader Ralf Dekker told Volkskrant he had not heard the episode. The podcast gives a platform to voices that “provoke thought”, he said, “and then it can sometimes be outlandish. But if this was said literally, I do not agree with it.” He said there was no reason to remove it: “You should never take anything offline.”

Laughland and the FvD press office have not responded to questions from Volkskrant since Friday.

Léonie de Jonge, a political scientist who researches the far right, told the paper the English-language format was no accident: the podcast is aimed at international far-right networks, not Dutch voters. Anthropologist Amade M’charek said “feeble-minded” is a eugenics term used to justify mass sterilisation in the 20th century.

Earlier episodes have featured guests defending the “great replacement” conspiracy theory, and Laughland himself has spoken of a “horrible cabal” transferring wealth to a small elite, a phrase closely tied to antisemitic conspiracy theories, Volkskrant said.

Laughland, who taught Baudet at Oxford, worked from 2008 to 2015 for a Russian-funded think tank in Paris. Investigative platform Follow the Money reported last year that he spoke at four Russian government-linked conferences between June 2024 and May 2025, with his travel and accommodation paid by his Russian hosts, which the FvD confirmed. He has described Ukraine as “a fiction”.

World.title: Dutch asylum numbers a third lower than a year ago
World.content:
The number of people registering for asylum in the Netherlands has fallen below 600 a week for the first time this year, according to weekly figures from the asylum ministry.

The drop is heavy compared to last year, when for most of autumn 2025 the weekly total was around 1,000, Volkskrant reported on Thursday.

The drop in numbers is mostly down to a reduction in family reunification requests. The number of relatives arriving to join people who already have refugee status has dropped from around 300 a week before the summer to between 110 and 120 a week over the past fortnight.

Syrians

The Netherlands has recorded more than 40,000 asylum-related arrivals every year since 2022. New applications fell sharply after the collapse of the Assad regime in Syria in December 2024, but the total stayed roughly level because Syrians who already had refugee status were still bringing over their families.

A record 16,500 family members arrived in 2025, up 39% on the year before, and three-quarters of them were Syrian, according to statistics agency CBS.

Tighter EU rules on family reunification came into force in June under the European migration pact. The ministry has not yet said what is behind the drop.

Senate

The ministry has only published a breakdown of the weekly figures since late June. Until then its weekly press release was a single line giving one total for new applications, repeat applications, resettlement and family members combined.

Applications are reportedly falling across Europe. The EU asylum agency EUAA said last week that the 27 member states plus Norway and Switzerland received 332,000 applications in the first half of 2026, 17% fewer than a year earlier and the lowest first-half total since 2021.

The agency attributed much of the drop to fewer applications from Venezuelans and Syrians.

World.title: Nearly a quarter of children in NL have divorced parents
World.content:

New research shows that 24% of 15-year-olds have parents who are no longer together, just a slight increase from a decade ago, according to statistics bureau CBS.

In 2025, 3.3 million children were living in the Netherlands. Around 782,000 had parents who are separated.

Twenty years ago, around 13% of 15-year-olds had divorced parents. That number increased steadily, reaching 23% in 2016, when it plateaued.

Most children of separated parents lived with their mother, particularly the youngest: 93% of 4-year-olds, falling to 83% by the age of 17.

Since 1995, the number of children with same-sex parents has also increased. In 1995, around 1,000 children had two legal mothers. By 2025, that number was more than 12,000. There are far fewer children with two legal fathers, just 500 in 2025.

The number of parents who never marry has increased sharply in the last 30 years. In 1995, of 15-year-olds with two legal parents, 80% lived with their married legal parents. Only 1,500 children of that age lived with unmarried parents.

By 2025, that share had fallen to 54.7%.

World.title: Unemployment virtually unchanged in August
World.content:
The unemployment rate remained at 4% in August, the same as July, with around 408,000 people out of work, according to new figures from Dutch statistics bureau CBS.

While the total number of unemployed people in the Netherlands has risen, on average, by around 3,000 per month since June, the number of people leaving the labour force has also increased.

During the same time period, the number of people outside the labour force decreased by an average of 4,000 per month. Retirees and those who are unable to work due to disability or illness make up the majority of the non-labour force.

Since 2023, the number of unemployed people in the Netherlands has been slowly rising. In April, 343,000 were unemployed.

The Dutch unemployment agency UWV registered around 195,000 people on unemployment benefits. That was slightly higher, around 1.4%, than it was in July.

World.title: Netherlands slips again in global gender equality ranking
World.content:

The Netherlands has fallen three places to 46th out of 145 countries in the World Economic Forum’s Global Gender Gap Index, a year after dropping 15 places to 43rd.

The annual index measures the gap between men and women on economic participation, education, health and political influence.

The Netherlands has closed 75% of its gap, down 0.6 percentage points on last year, according to the University of Amsterdam team that compiled the Dutch data.

There is no longer a gap in education or health and the economic score has risen slightly, but neighbouring countries are moving faster, Henk Volberda, the UvA professor who led the research, told broadcaster NOS.

The main drag is politics: the share of women in parliament rose slightly but the number of women ministers fell, and the country has never had a female prime minister.

“I thought we had hit rock bottom last year,” Volberda said. He argued that nobody in government feels responsible for the issue, which sits with the education ministry, and wants quotas for senior public and corporate posts along with Scandinavian-style free childcare and longer maternity leave.

Iceland tops the ranking, followed by Finland, Norway, Namibia and the UK. Germany is ninth. The Netherlands was in the top 15 almost every year between 2006 and 2016.

World.title: Opposition urge cabinet to pick a route as budget debate begins
World.content:
The left-wing opposition party Pro is willing to talk to the coalition parties about reducing healthcare costs, but only if the cabinet abandons its €6.5 billion cuts to welfare spending, party leader Jesse Klaver said on the first day of the Dutch budget debate.

Klaver said it would be a “scandal” if the government fell over its first budget, but he also pressed Rob Jetten’s administration to make up its mind whether to seek support from left or right.

As the first speaker in the two-day debate on finance minister Eelco Heinen’s budget, Klaver said his party wanted to break the deadlock that led to pre-budget talks breaking down.

“After so much political unrest in recent years, I think it is in all our interests that this cabinet succeeds,” he said. “Sometimes I think the opposition is keener to make it a success than the coalition parties themselves.”

Jan Paternotte, leader of the largest coalition party D66, called on parties on all sides to work on a budget with broad appeal and look beyond “the left-right discussion in The Hague”.

But his words found little support from the opposition, which accused the coalition of D66, CDA and VVD of lacking leadership. “What kind of road map does the cabinet see before it?” Mirjam Bikker, leader of the ChristenUnie, asked.

The three parties have 66 seats in the lower house, 10 short of a majority, while in the Senate they need to find 16 extra votes to pass their legislation.

No perfect match

Pro, with 20 seats in the lower house and 14 senators, provides the most straightforward route, but the right-wing VVD is reluctant to make too many concessions to the left and favours a deal with parties such as JA21 and the orthodox Protestant SGP.

Paternotte said the coalition wanted to continue talking to parties on all sides in the coming weeks. “The perfect political match doesn’t exist, only the will to come to an agreement. My invitation stands.”

Klaver himself came in for criticism from other opposition leaders who said the proposed budget deal had already made too many concessions to the left.

Joost Eerdmans, leader of the hardline conservative JA21, said the cabinet needed to “make the choice” between his party and Pro rather than trying to reach out to both.

In contrast to Pro, JA21 argues the cabinet should cut even more from the welfare bill to create room in the budget for tax cuts and measures to ease the cost of living.

Eerdmans also said plans to invest billions in climate change measures should be redirected to help working families. “The idea that we can change the world’s climate is unrealistic,” he said.

Two budgets

Eerdmans suggested to Paternotte that the cabinet should write two budgets, one for the left-wing parties and one for the right, and let MPs debate them both.

But Paternotte urged Eerdmans to “take off the rose-tinted glasses”. “How does that get you to a majority in the Senate?” he said. “Pro or JA21 on their own aren’t enough.”

Klaver’s pitch to the cabinet also prompted Socialist Party leader Jimmy Dijk to ask how far Pro was willing to compromise on healthcare spending.

Pro would not “work to break things down”, Klaver replied, but he saw potential to make savings by tackling “all kinds of treatments that aren’t necessary” and “taking the market out of youth care”.

Draft published

Paternotte also said D66 was willing to discuss surrogate parenthood with the SGP, which wants the cabinet to block any moves to legalise the practice as a condition for its support.

MPs also voted to ask the cabinet to publish the original draft budget by finance minister Eelco Heinen which was rejected by his coalition partners, prompting an extra weekend of negotiations.

NRC reported that the original version preserved most of the plans to cut welfare spending, despite Pro pressing for them to be taken off the table. In both the draft and the final version Heinen proposed delaying around half the cuts by a year.

Warsaw has launched special joint patrols by its municipal police and roads authority to check whether electric scooters are being parked legally and in keeping with rules introduced under a recent agreement with rental firms. According to the city’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, more than 140 improperly parked scooters have been towed away within just a few days. Under the agreement, their operators now face potential fines. Nie ma miejsca dla hulajnóg tam, gdzie nie ich miejsce. Zdecydowałem o uruchomieniu specjalnych patroli Straży Miejskiej i ZDM. W ciągu ostatnich kliku dni dzięki ich pracy odholowanych zostało ponad 140 nieprawidłowo zaparkowanych hulajnóg elektrycznych. Taką możliwość daje… pic.twitter.com/U5fd7YDN8U — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) September 16, 2026 “There’s no place for scooters where they don’t belong,” Trzaskowski said in a social media post announcing the patrols. “There are specific provisions, agreements and legal regulations – and action is being taken. No leniency.” An agreement reached between the city and three scooter operators – Bolt, Dott and Lime – in May expanded the number of streets where the vehicles are subject to a maximum speed of 12 km/h (7.5 mph) and increased the areas where their use is entirely prohibited. It also introduced measures to prevent scooters from being left in places where parking is illegal. Riding and parking electric scooters was banned in several areas of Warsaw, including popular tourist attractions such as the Old Town, Krasiński Garden and Łazienki Park. Trzaskowski added that the city has now expanded the list of areas covered by the ban, as permitted under the agreement. He did not, however, provide the new list. The agreement requires operators to programme their scooters so they cannot enter areas where riding is prohibited or be parked in places where parking is illegal, including on bridges, in tunnels, in residential areas and on streets where the pavement is too narrow to allow legal parking. Operators can be fined when scooters are left in violation of the rules. The city says that, despite electric scooters accounting for just under 8% of all traffic on cycle lanes, their riders were found to be responsible for 39 of the 66 accidents recorded on cycle lanes last year. Those accidents resulted in 73 injuries. Concerns over the safety of electric scooters have also prompted the national government to introduce stricter rules, including a nationwide requirement for children under 16 to wear a bicycle helmet when riding bicycles and electric scooters, which took effect in early June. Poland first introduced regulations governing electric scooters in 2021, formally setting out rules for their use. Under those rules, scooters are generally required to use cycle lanes where available, with their maximum speed capped at 20 km/h. The Polish government has moved to introduce new rules on the use of electric scooters. E-scooters, which are currently unregulated in Poland, have been blamed for hundreds of accidents annually, with half of victims being pedestrians hit by riders https://t.co/TcrfPQocfr — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 3, 2021 Under the nationwide legislation, electric scooters must be parked parallel to the outer edge of the pavement, and municipal authorities have the power to penalise those responsible for improper parking – a provision that primarily affects rental companies. A year after the legislation was introduced, after the first report on e-scooter-related accidents showed that they had caused hundreds of injuries and three deaths in 2021, Poland’s police launched a campaign publicising the new rules. At national level, infrastructure minister Dariusz Klimczak has announced further restrictions the government is working on, including a new law requiring scooters to be collected and left only in specially designated zones. The police have launched a campaign on the legal requirements for using e-scooters, including a warning that riding or parking them on pavements can be illegal. World.title: Polish right-wing opposition MPs call for Independence Day march in Ukrainian city of Lviv
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A group of MPs from Poland’s main right-wing and far-right opposition parties have jointly called on the government to organise a march on Polish Independence Day in the Ukrainian city of Lviv, which was historically part of Poland. The idea has been firmly rejected by figures from the ruling coalition, who have called it “gross stupidity” and “madness”. It is also unclear to what extent the leadership of the opposition parties support the proposal. Pomysł zorganizowania "polskiego Marszu Niepodległości ulicami Lwowa" połączył polityków całej prawicy: PiS, Konfederacji, Rozwoju Plus i Konfederacji Korony Polskiej. Odsłaniamy kulisy. Pisze @patrykmichalski, autor programu #NewsMichalskiego ⤵️ 🔵 https://t.co/9L0M5lN0zY pic.twitter.com/1W3YxHdXHT — TVN24+ (@tvn24plus) September 15, 2026 The suggestion was made in a so-called parliamentary interpellation – through which MPs can ask questions and make suggestions to the government – submitted this month and signed by a group of 21 opposition MPs. They called on the government to do more to support the ethnic Polish community that still lives in Lviv, arguing that neither the Polish nor the Ukrainian state does enough to help them preserve and celebrate their identity. By contrast, argued the signatories, Polish state entities provide funding for Ukrainian organisations and events in Poland, including celebrations of Ukrainian Independence Day on 24 August. As such, they called upon the government to “organise official celebrations of [Polish] Independence Day in Lviv, including a Polish Independence March through the streets of the city” on 11 November. This would be “a concrete sign of remembrance and solidarity with Poles living in Ukraine”. Among the 21 signatories, 14 are from the caucus of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s ruling party between 2015 and 2023 and now the largest opposition group. A further three are from Confederation (Konfederacja), a far-right opposition group. One is from Development Plus (Rozwój Plus), a group that broke away from PiS earlier this year; another is from Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), a radical-right, pro-Russian party led by Grzegorz Braun. The final two are an independent, Janusz Kowalski, who recently quit PiS; and Jarosław Sachajko, who was elected in 2023 on the PiS party list but is part of the small Direct Democracy (Demokracja Bezpośrednia) group associated with Paweł Kukiz, a right-wing, anti-establishment figure. Interpelacja do Prezesa Rady Ministrów w sprawie zorganizowania 11 listopada polskiego Marszu Niepodległości ulicami Lwowa 11 listopada Rzeczpospolita Polska obchodzi Narodowe Święto Niepodległości. Jest to święto wszystkich Polaków, również tych, którzy mieszkają poza granicami… pic.twitter.com/7m6yUg1iKZ — Dariusz Matecki (@DariuszMatecki) August 25, 2026 It remains unclear to what extent the MPs have the backing of their parties in calling for the government to organise an Independence Day march in Lviv. Indeed, when Krzysztof Bosak, one of the leaders of Confederation, was asked about the idea on Wednesday, he appeared to know very little about it. Speaking to broadcaster RMF, Bosak said that he had first heard about the proposal on Tuesday and that, after looking into it, he said it appeared to be a “stunt”, and one that he felt was “unnecessary”. “I think the point is to draw attention to the fact that Polish institutions are participating in the celebration of Ukraine’s Independence Day in Warsaw, and that there should be some symmetry,” said Bosak. However, he added that he felt many people would not understand this intention. “The appeal should be directed at Ukrainian institutions, not the Polish foreign ministry,” he said, adding that the MPs who came up with the idea should better explain it. “Frankly, I have more serious matters to attend to.” Czy przemarsz Polaków ulicami Lwowa z okazji Dnia Niepodległości to dobry pomysł? Zdaniem @krzysztofbosak niepotrzebny, a traktować go należy w kategorii happeningu. Ale jeśli się trzymać zasady wzajemności, to już lepiej organizować coś podobnego… w Kijowie. pic.twitter.com/PxdqNKBlCC — Ekonomat (@ekonomat_pl) September 16, 2026 Throughout much of history, Lviv (known in Polish as Lwów) was part of the Polish state, most recently during the period between the First and Second World Wars. However, amid postwar border movements, it became part of Ukraine along with some other former Polish territories. Many in Poland still feel a sense of attachment to the former Polish “borderlands” (kresy) that are now located in Ukraine, Lithuania and Belarus, and which are still home to at least hundreds of thousands of ethnic Poles (though the exact number is a matter of dispute). In Lviv itself, the most recent Ukrainian national census, taken in 2001, showed just under 10,000 people declaring Polish ethnicity in the city (around 1% of the population), though some estimates put the figure higher. Poland's culture minister has condemned Russia's attacks on the historic centre of Lviv in Ukraine, a UNESCO World Heritage site. She noted that Lviv, which was once part of Poland, represents the "shared history of Ukraine, Poland and all of Europe" https://t.co/qPhqXMAZ9r — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 25, 2026 Last year, Confederation’s other main leader, Sławomir Mentzen, clashed with the mayor of Lviv, Andriy Sadovyi, after visiting the city and criticising a monument commemorating nationalist leader Stepan Bandera, a figure seen as a hero by many in Ukraine but regarded as a war criminal in Poland. Followers of Bandera were responsible for the so-called Volhynia massacres during World War Two, in which Ukrainian nationalists massacred around 100,000 ethnic Polish civilians. Poland regards the killings as a genocide but Ukraine rejects that label. The issue has caused renewed tension this year after President Volodymyr Zelensky named a Ukrainian military unit after the “heroes of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army”, which led the massacres. Any Polish attempt at a state-backed Independence Day march in Ukraine would likely stir further controversy. A leading candidate in Poland’s presidential election has clashed with a Ukrainian mayor after visiting his city and criticising the presence of a monument to Stepan Bandera, who is seen as a hero by many in Ukraine but regarded as a war criminal in Poland https://t.co/nA9JzMmBcg — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 26, 2025 Although the Polish government has not yet officially responded to the opposition MPs’ interpellation, a number of figures from the ruling coalition – which ranges from left to centre right – criticised the idea on Wednesday. Deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk called it “gross stupidity” to think of organising such a march in Ukraine, especially at a time of war. He asked how Poles would feel if Germany tried to organise a similar march in Poland (some of whose current territory was part of Germany before World War Two). Both Dariusz Wieczorek, an MP from The Left (Lewica), and Marek Biernacki from the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL) told broadcaster TVN that the idea was “madness”. Próba zorganizowania we Lwowie prawicowej prowokacji z udziałem PiS-u, Rozwój Plus i Brauna to jednoznaczne działanie na rzecz Rosji i przeciwko polskiej racji stanu. — Witold Zembaczyński🇵🇱 (@WZembaczynski) September 16, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: European Parliament strips Polish far-right leader of immunity to face Holocaust denial charge
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The European Parliament has again stripped Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun of legal immunity to face charges in his homeland of denying Nazi crimes, an offence that carries a potential prison sentence of up to three years. The decision marks the sixth time that the European Parliament has lifted Braun’s immunity, and the second time for charges of Holocaust denial. Braun is already on trial in Poland for an attack on a Jewish religious celebration in parliament and is facing a number of other legal cases. Parlament Europejski w głosowaniu w Strasburgu uchylił immunitet europosła Grzegorza Brauna. Sprawa dotyczy negowania przez niego Holokaustu. Więcej: https://t.co/rB3UPUiS8o pic.twitter.com/icRLEqsWmF — Gazeta.pl (@gazetapl_news) September 15, 2026 In a vote on Tuesday, a majority of MEPs voted in favour of a request, submitted in February by Poland’s justice minister, Waldemar Żurek, to lift the immunity enjoyed by Braun as an MEP. He has sat in the European Parliament since being elected in 2024. In his request, Żurek said that Polish prosecutors wish to charge Braun in relation to “denial of genocide crimes committed by functionaries of the Third Reich in the Auschwitz-Birkenau concentration camp and the Lublin concentration camp (Majdanek)”. Poland’s Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), a state historical body that has prosecutorial power, also revealed that the accusation relates to the use of gas chambers at those two camps. Neither the IPN nor Żurek confirmed at the time what specific words Braun had said that prompted the planned charges against him. However, the IPN noted that they had come at a live event broadcast online on 27 September 2025. On that date, Braun took part in a discussion with Jan Żaryn, a right-wing historian and former senator for the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party, titled “The Polish Underground State and the Jewish Issue”. A recording of the event is still available online. During his remarks, Braun referred to the “fake gas chambers of Majdanek and Auschwitz”, calling them “a dark, monstrous fantasy that has no satisfactory historical or academic support”. He suggested that the idea of the gas chambers had been invented as part of “propaganda and black PR operations conducted by the Soviet and Anglo-Saxon security services during World War Two”, and that the false claim continues to be exploited by Jews today. The European Parliament has again voted to strip Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun of immunity to face further charges for Holocaust denial as well as various antisemitic, anti-Ukrainian and anti-LGBT incidents during last year's presidential campaign https://t.co/4EHVEuSDnM — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 26, 2026 In actual fact, historians estimate that around 900,000 people were killed in the gas chambers at Auschwitz. The vast majority were Jews, but victims also included Roma, Soviet prisoners of war, and ethnic Poles. Meanwhile, gas chambers at Majdanek were used to kill tens of thousands, again mainly Jews. Today, the ashes of the camp’s cremated victims are preserved in a memorial at the site of the former camp. Braun, who has a long history of promoting antisemitic conspiracy theories, has repeatedly sought to cast doubt on the veracity of Nazi crimes against Jews. Last month, he was charged with denying Nazi crimes in a separate case over earlier comments in which he called Auschwitz’s gas chambers “fake”. Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun has been charged with denying Nazi crimes, a criminal offence in Poland that carries a prison sentence of up to three years, for statements he made suggesting that the gas chambers at Auschwitz are "fake" https://t.co/PCssZt5eXD — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 25, 2026 In December, Braun went on trial over a separate set of charges relating to four other incidents, including his attack on a celebration of the Jewish festival of Hanukkah in parliament in December 2023 and his disruption of a lecture by a Holocaust scholar. “I am standing before this court because I dared to defend myself against oppression and the ritual manifestation of Jewish supremacy,” declared Braun at the start of the trial, which remains ongoing. Braun is also facing various legal cases relating to his anti-Ukrainian and anti-LGBT actions. Last week, he posted a video of himself using a hammer to vandalise a monument in Poland dedicated to the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA). Police are investigating that incident. Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun has published a video of himself using a hammer to attack a monument in Poland to soldiers from the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, a WWII group that fought against the Soviets but was also responsible for massacring Poles https://t.co/oCYRtNRO9N — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 11, 2026 Braun’s high-profile stunts have seen his popularity surge among a section of the electorate. He finished a surprise fourth in last year’s Polish presidential election, with over 6% of the vote, and his Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) party is now polling around 8-9%. If it manages to secure that level of support at next year’s parliamentary elections, KKP could become a key player in deciding what kind of government can be formed after what looks likely to be a very close contest between the ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, and the right-wing and far-right opposition. An MEP from the ruling coalition, Michał Kobosko, welcomed Tuesday’s decision to lift Braun’s immunity, saying that the far-right leader “deliberately and consciously…stokes hatred”. Kobosko said that such actions are particularly dangerous at a time when Russia is “actively waging hybrid and cognitive war against Poland”. He noted that Braun and his party have taken a sympathetic position towards Russia, including calling for Poland to “normalise” relations with Moscow. Figures from Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun's party celebrated Russia Day at the Russian embassy and presented a letter hailing Russia's development, blaming "globalists" for the Ukraine war and calling for normalisation of Polish-Russian relations https://t.co/SU3gEdVod0 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 13, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: China overtakes Germany as Poland’s biggest source of imports for first time
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. China overtook Germany to become Poland’s biggest source of imports for the first time in July, according to new data from the central bank. It ends a period of around 35 years in which Germany had consistently held top spot. The shift came as imports of Chinese goods surged, driven in part by a sharp increase in Chinese cars, while imports from Germany declined. “In July 2026, China was the largest supplier of goods to Poland for the first time, overtaking Germany in that month,” wrote the National Bank of Poland (NBP) in an announcement on Monday. “A significant increase in imports of computer hardware, passenger cars and durable consumer goods influenced the shift in the geographical structure of imports,” added the bank. Znamy już pełne dane handlowe za lipiec 2026 – za miesiąc kiedy Chiny po raz pierwszy w historii stały się największym dostawcą towarów do Polski, przed Niemcami. W lipcu import ogółem z Chin wzrósł o 28,8% r/r, podczas gdy z Niemiec spadł o 1,8% r/r. Import pojazdów… pic.twitter.com/LfJ50nXzNM — PKO Research (@PKO_Research) September 15, 2026 In a comment on the new data, analysts at PKO, a Polish bank, said that the July shift was partly due to “one-time factors” and noted that Germany remains Poland’s largest supplier on a 12-month basis, although its lead has been steadily shrinking. In July, Polish imports from China rose 28.8% year-on-year, while imports from Germany fell 1.8%, according to PKO. Imports of motor vehicles from Germany fell 9.3% year-on-year, while imports from China rose 54.4%. Imports from China of computers, electronics and optical equipment rose 31.5% year-on-year in July, the strongest increase since 2022. More detailed data on trade with the two countries, published also on Tuesday by Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, provided further insight into the shift. According to GUS, Poland imported goods worth €36.7 billion from China in the first seven months of the year, giving China a 15.9% share of total Polish imports, up from 14.9% in the same period of 2025. Imports from Germany stood at €43.1 billion in that period, 18.6% of the total, down from 19.4% in 2025. Poland’s third-largest source of imports was the United States, with €12.7 worth of goods, a share of 5.5%, up from 4.9% in 2025. Poland has been NATO's biggest importer of arms over the last five years, according to new data from @SIPRIorg. Over 90% of Polish imports have come from South Korea and the United States https://t.co/jij0nfbhFc — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 9, 2026 Germany has been Poland’s largest trading partner since the collapse of communism, leading both in imports and exports. It overtook the Soviet Union, which had dominated Poland’s foreign trade during the communist era. But China has steadily gained ground as a source of Polish imports since the 2010s, rising to second place behind Germany by the 2020s. In terms of exports in the first seven months of this year, Germany dominates, receiving goods worth €69.8 billion, or 26.3% of all Poland’s exports. It is followed by the Czech Republic (€14.3 billion), France (€14.0 billion), the United Kingdom (€11.6 billion) and the Netherlands (€10.9 billion). World.title: Polish PM condemns “disgrace” of failed Venezuela oil deal under former government following FT report
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. Prime Minister Donald Tusk says that Poland has been “disgraced in front of the entire world” by a new Financial Times report on how Polish state energy firm Orlen lost $230 million (856 million zloty) trying to buy Venezuelan oil through intermediaries, unsecured payments and cryptocurrency transfers. Tusk called the case a further example of “dirty deals” conducted under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which was in power at the time. Orlen was then led by Daniel Obajtek, who is now a member of the European Parliament representing PiS. Obajtek himself today said that he wants the issue to be clarified in court and suggested that the current authorities are using the case to distract from current soaring fuel prices. How Poland lost $230mn trying to buy Venezuelan oil with crypto https://t.co/Xo07JkYy1t — Financial Times (@FT) September 15, 2026 In a report today, the FT provided new details on a case that has already drawn public attention in Poland. In April 2024, Orlen revealed that its Swiss oil trading subsidiary had lost around $400 million in prepayments for Venezuelan oil and petroleum products that were never delivered. Orlen, which was under new management after Obajtek had been fired earlier that year following the arrival of Tusk’s government, said that the losses included around $240 million paid to a Dubai-based intermediary run by a 25-year-old from Hong Kong. A week later, Polish prosecutors announced that they had launched an investigation into the case, focusing on Orlen Trading Switzerland (OTS), the subsidiary that oversaw the Venezuela deal. Polish prosecutors have launched an investigation into OTS, @GrupaORLEN's Swiss subsidiary which had lost $400 million on prepayments for oil that was never delivered. It also announced that the homes of Orlen's former senior management had been searchedhttps://t.co/QQ5QJMsHg4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 1, 2024 The FT detailed how the then head of OTS, a Lebanese-born Polish citizen of Palestinian descent, who can be named only as Samer A. under Polish privacy law, had sought in 2023 to commission the import of Venezuelan oil through intermediaries, who were given a $230 million advance without any security or guarantees. Although the United States, under then-President Joe Biden, had temporarily suspended sanctions on Venezuelan oil, allowing companies such as Orlen to buy it, Venezuela’s state oil company, PDVSA, remained largely cut off from the global financial system. The FT detailed how the intermediaries therefore sought to use cryptocurrency to facilitate the deal. However, although oil tankers leased by Orlen to collect the oil sat waiting (accruing further large costs), the promised oil was not delivered, and Orlen’s advance payments were lost. The issue is now the subject of a criminal investigation in Poland and an ongoing arbitration case with the intermediary in Dubai, Hannon International. Speaking ahead of a meeting of his cabinet on Tuesday, Tusk said that the FT story is a “disgrace in front of the entire world”. He called the Venezuelan oil incident “the biggest scandal, or one of the biggest scandals, in our country’s history”. Turning his aim on the opposition, he said that the case includes “everything that has recently been associated with PiS”, including “dirty deals” and cryptocurrencies. That was a reference to an ongoing investigation into alleged links between a collapsed crypto firm, Zondacrypto, and figures associated with the opposition. Tusk also noted that opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki has recently blocked government bills intended to better regulate crypto markets and to levy a windfall tax on fuel firms. “We may be dealing with a network of dirty and highly dangerous dealings,” said the prime minister. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk: Cała Polska dzisiaj to komentuje. Wstyd na cały świat. Financial Times pisze o jednym z największych skandali w historii naszego kraju i cały świat dzisiaj o tym czyta. pic.twitter.com/Ej17Csi4DL — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) September 15, 2026 Later on Tuesday, the regional prosecutor’s office in Warsaw also responded to the FT article by issuing a statement providing an update on the investigation into the Venezuelan oil deal. They noted that the Polish authorities are continuing to seek the extradition of Samer A. from the United Arab Emirates, which last year rejected a request from Poland for him to be extradited. The prosecutors also reported today that, last month, they issued indictments against three former senior Orlen and OTS executives for failing to fulfil their duties to oversee the companies’ assets, resulting in losses of $378 million. Prosecutors have charged the former head of the charitable foundation of Polish state energy giant Orlen for allowing its funds to be used to support a political campaign of the former ruling PiS party in violation of the foundation's statute https://t.co/w1Xtmivn0I — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 6, 2026 Obajtek himself responded to the FT’s story, writing on social media that the newspaper “describes an important part of the OTS case”. He then suggested that the new management of OTS had terminated the Venezuelan oil contract too quickly, saying that the oil could in fact have been delivered. “I hope this matter will be fully clarified, including before a Polish court!” wrote Obajtek. In a further post, he suggested that Orlen and the authorities are “trying to cover up current issues again, such as the most expensive fuel in history”. In response, Orlen’s press office wrote under one of Obajtek’s posts that they would “help [him] with English”. “The article is about how your team transferred hundreds of millions of dollars to a company owned by a 25-year-old from Dubai. He converted them into cryptocurrencies, which he copied onto USB drives. And then he handed them out in restaurants to people posing as oil traders…In this story, only Orlen’s money, which they lost, was real.” Panie Pośle, pomożemy z angielskim. Artykuł jest o tym, jak pana ekipa przelała setki milionów dolarów do firmy 25-latka z Dubaju. On zamienił je na kryptowaluty, które zgrał na pendrivy. A później rozdawał w restauracjach ludziom, podającym się za handlarzy ropą. To jak „kupić”… — Biuro Prasowe ORLEN (@b_prasoweORLEN) September 15, 2026 Obajtek rose rapidly under the former PiS government, which ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023. He went from being the mayor of Pcim, a rural commune of 11,000 people in southern Poland, to the CEO of Orlen, Poland’s biggest company, in the space of three years. Under Obajtek’s leadership, Orlen expanded rapidly, swallowing up other state energy firms and expanding into new areas of activity. By 2023, it was ranked among Europe’s 50 biggest companies. However, Obajtek was also accused of using the company’s considerable resources to support PiS politically, including through Orlen’s purchases of hundreds of local media outlets – many of whose editors were replaced with PiS-friendly figures – and lowering fuel prices ahead of the 2023 elections. Last year, at Poland’s request, the European Parliament stripped Obajtek of legal immunity to face charges for allegedly using Orlen’s funds to serve his own private interests. Polish prosecutors are also pursuing him for allegedly violating Poland’s press law and falsely reporting his income in a tax return. World.title: “Don’t be a creep”: Polish ice cream company launches campaign against sexual harassment of staff
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A Polish ice cream chain has launched a campaign to stamp out sexual harassment of staff by customers, including empowering employees to refuse to serve such clients. The campaign is based around the fact that the Polish word for ice cream, “lody”, also has an informal vulgar meaning, referring to oral sex. The company, Good Lood, which runs 37 outlets, says that its female staff regularly suffer lewd comments from male customers incorporating this double entendre. In response, in late August it launched a campaign titled “Nie bądź oblechem”, meaning “Don’t be a creep”, with information displayed prominently at its ice cream stands and on its social media platforms. The firm said it condemned “crude remarks, inappropriate jokes and verbal harassment directed at service workers” and promised to support its staff in dealing with them. “Everyone deserves respect, without exception!” Good Lood advised employees to respond to inappropriate comments with a short, firm retort such as “Great, that’s the 20th time I’ve heard that” or “Perhaps you could repeat that more loudly, so the rest of the queue can hear?” It also called on other customers to react if they witnessed such behaviour. In a follow-up social media post last week, the company confirmed that staff had its backing if they decided not to serve a customer. “If someone is a creep and makes inappropriate comments and verbally harasses them, our team have the right to refuse them service.” That post alone has so far garnered more than 50,000 likes or other positive responses on Facebook. Good Lood says that its messages posted as part of the campaign have already received over 10 million organic views on social media. Comments on the company’s posts show overwhelming support, with many commenters sharing their own experiences. “At last someone has spoken out about this!” wrote one, who said she worked in an ice cream parlour as a teenager. “I remember how outraged I felt when I heard comments like that from men who could have been my fathers, or even my grandfathers. I wonder what would happen if someone spoke to their daughters or granddaughters like that.” Good Lood says it want to start a broader conversation on the “global issue” of harassment and disrespect towards front-line staff in retail and hospitality. “Working in service or hospitality does not mean consenting to disrespect. The safety and wellbeing of our team will always come before profit. We are not afraid to lose a customer who cannot show basic human respect,” the company said in a press release. Founded 10 years ago in Kraków, Good Lood now has 37 outlets there as well as in the Warsaw area. It also sells its products throughout Poland at Biedronka, the country’s largest supermarket chain. Poland’s interior ministry has launched a TV campaign, including spots on public broadcaster TVP’s flagship morning show, aimed at educating the public about how to respond to emergency situations such as natural disasters and security threats. The initiative comes as Poland has faced growing threats from Russia, including acts of sabotage and the entry of missiles and drones into Polish airspace. Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned this week that there may be an “escalation” of such actions in the coming weeks and months. 📺 Dzisiejsza wizyta w programie „Pytanie na Śniadanie” odbyła się w ramach naszej nowej kampanii „ Minuta dla twojego bezpieczeństwa”! Rozmawialiśmy o sprawach fundamentalnych – o bezpieczeństwie. Mogliście sprawdzić, czy wiecie, co oznaczają sygnały alarmowe oraz krok po kroku… pic.twitter.com/ARta1Pqmlz — MSWiA 🇵🇱 (@MSWiA_GOV_PL) September 8, 2026 The new campaign will include weekend segments on the TVP1 channel and a series of pieces aired during TVP2’s breakfast show, Pytanie na śniadanie, which had an average audience of 322,000 in August, according to Nielsen Media data. The weekend programmes will introduce topics such as floods, fires, extreme weather, power outages, chemical contamination, evacuation, cybersecurity, disinformation and first aid. Specialists will then discuss the subjects in greater detail during the morning segments. The ministry says the content is based on its official security handbook, which it sent to all 17 million Polish households earlier this year, and is intended to help people prepare for emergencies before they occur. “We only find out whether we’re prepared for difficult situations when they actually arise,” said Mateusz Jarecki, who is presenting the segments. “That’s why, in collaboration with specialists, we’ve produced a series of short, easy-to-follow videos that will help you prepare for various life scenarios.” The government is sending copies of a booklet advising how to prepare for and act in emergencies to all 17 million households in Poland. World.title: Moose on the loose at Warsaw’s main station brings trains to a standstill
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A moose wandered onto the tracks at Warsaw Central Station on Sunday evening, disrupting rail services in the Polish capital for more than 80 minutes before it was safely removed. The animal first appeared on a platform before moving onto the tracks, forcing Polish Railway Lines (PLK), the company responsible for Poland’s rail infrastructure, to suspend, cancel and divert several train services. View this post on Instagram A post shared by TVP3 Warszawa (@tvp3warszawa) Videos and photographs shared online showed the moose lying on the tracks and running along the railway line at Warsaw Central, the capital’s busiest station, which is mainly underground and therefore not easy for such a large animal to access. Police do not know how the moose ended up at the station, reports broadcaster TVN24. Officers were first alerted at 7:10 pm on Sunday and cordoned off the platform where the animal was located. When emergency services arrived, the moose was tranquilised. It was then placed on a large sheet and carried out of the station by police officers and emergency workers before being loaded onto a specialist vehicle to be returned to a forested area. PLK, which named the moose Emil, later confirmed that the animal had been safely removed and that normal train services were being restored. The company added that the disruptions lasted just over 80 minutes, using a pun combining the Polish words for moose (łoś) and 80 (osiemdziesiąt) to produce the word “łosiemdziesiąt”. ❗Aktualizacja❗Zwierze zostało bezpiecznie zabrane z torów. Przywracana jest rozkładowa organizacja ruchu pociągów. Utrudnienia trwały przeszło łosiemdziesiąt minut. https://t.co/Xui2B6SxyU — PLK SA (@PKP_PLK_SA) September 13, 2026 The Eurasian moose (also known as the Eurasian elk) has long been native to Poland, but by the mid-20th century hunting and habitat loss had brought the species close to extinction in the country. Its population subsequently recovered, reaching an estimated 6,000 animals by the 1980s and around 30,000 by 2019, helped by a moratorium on moose hunting introduced in 2001. Several hundred live in the Kampinos national park on the northwestern outskirts of Warsaw. They are therefore relatively frequent visitors to the capital, according to the Interia news website, although venturing onto train lines in the centre is unusual. The growth in the moose population, combined with urban expansion and changes to its habitat, has led to other high-profile encounters in areas inhabited by humans. In 2022, a moose was spotted on the roof of a shopping centre in the northern Polish city of Elbląg. A moose was this morning spotted on the roof of a shopping centre in Poland.
