World.title: How Diaspora Professionals Use Croatian Citizenship to Work in Europe’s Top Hubs
World.content:
September the 17th, 2026 – The Croatian diaspora is vast, and many professionals are using their right to obtain Croatian citizenship as a key to unlocking work in Europe’s top hubs.

If we sift back through time, we’ll notice that the overarching pitch for securing Croatian citizenship by descent has targeted two distinct groups: those with a mysterious granny from a now abandoned Dalmatian village seeking a sentimental connection to their ancestral homeland, and retirees with similar stories looking to stretch their 401k to the maximum in a sun-drenched, slow-paced Mediterranean paradise.

It isn’t that those reasons don’t still largely exist, but it has to be said that times move (and more and more quickly), bringing marked shifts for the diaspora. A totally different demographic is suddenly digging up dida’s old birth certificates from curious settlements few have ever heard of. They’re the young, ambitious US corporate professionals who, for whatever reason, aren’t quite ready to give up on the grind and embrace the pomalo lifestyle just yet. Faced with the infamously gruelling American corporate world, hyper-competitive job markets, and a desire for global experience, millennial and Gen-Z professionals are realising that a Croatian passport isn’t just a nod to their heritage and genetic makeup, it’s also the ultimate professional fast-track into the booming, wide open EU economy.

croatian citizenship as a way to clear the corporate visa wall and unlock the european dream

Ask any young American professional who has tried to land a job in London, Amsterdam, Paris, or Berlin about their experience, and they will tell you the same thing: the visa barrier is nearly insurmountable. For a European company to hire an American citizen, they must generally prove to their local government that no qualified EU citizen could fill the role. This requires months of bureaucratic red tape, thousands of euros in legal fees, and an incredibly patient HR department. Unless you are a C-suite executive or a highly specialised niche engineer, most corporate resumes with a “Requires Visa Sponsorship” box checked are filtered out by automated tracking software before a human ever lays eyes on them.

Pulling a trusty little Croatian passport out of your pocket completely demolishes this dizzyingly high wall.

Because Croatia is a full Member State of the European Union, Croatian citizens possess the absolute right to live, work, and do business in any of the 27 EU member states, completely visa-free. As a dual citizen, an American professional can apply for a corporate job in Dublin, Amsterdam, or Frankfurt exactly like a local. No sponsorship is required, no legal fees are incurred for the employer, and there are no bureaucratic delays.

trading the american “live to work” for the european “work to live”

The motivation for young Americans to make the leap across the Atlantic goes far beyond geographic novelty. It is a fundamental rejection of the “hustle culture” that dominates US corporate life. When American professionals leverage their Croatian citizenship to work in Western or Northern Europe, they enter a completely different professional landscape where things like mandatory paid time off are completely normal.

While the US remains the only advanced economy without guaranteed paid vacation, all EU countries legally mandate between 20 to 30 days of paid annual leave, and employees are fiercely encouraged to actually use them.

Then comes the strict work-life balance: Countries like France and the Netherlands have strict laws regarding the “right to disconnect,” making it illegal or completely culturally unacceptable for managers to email or call employees after standard working hours are over for the day.

Robust healthcare as a fundamental human right will also likely be music to the ears of any US citizen sick of paying an arm and a leg just in case they happen to become unwell. Health insurance ceases to be a terrifying golden handcuff tied to a specific, often exhausting job. Across Europe, high-quality healthcare is decoupled from employment status and heavily subsidised or entirely free at the point of use. No premiums, no back pay, and nobody has ever heard of the term “reaching their out of pocket maximum”.

career acceleration, all while exploring europe

Living and working abroad for two or three years isn’t a career pause, it’s a massive career accelerator, and you can do it all while enjoying free healthcare and actually being paid to sit back and relax. In an increasingly globalised economy, American companies place an immense premium on candidates with international operational experience. Navigating foreign markets, managing cross-cultural teams, and understanding EU regulatory landscapes (like GDPR) are skills that cannot be taught in any kind of US lecture hall. When a young professional decides to return to the US corporate ladder, a resume featuring a stint at a global hub in Munich or Amsterdam instantly stands out from a sea of applicants who have never left their home time zone.

how croatianbydescent.com can help you get the ball rolling

For young Americans, particularly those who barely have a second for themselves when they get home, the process of tracking down old archives, certifying documents, and dealing with troublesome Croatian ministries can feel daunting. Turning to not only experts, but members of the Croatian diaspora themselves who have personal experience of the process streamlines it all and makes you feel understood. It transforms journeying through sometimes complicated ancestral roots into a modern, powerful career tool.

It may never have really occurred to you outside of donning those checkers during the World Cup or enjoying a dish you struggle to pronounce that grandma used to make, but if you have a parent or grandparent who left Croatia, you aren’t just sitting on a family history. You might actually be sitting on the key to your next major career upgrade and a lifestyle that the USA could never realistically provide.

World.title: Dubrovnik Mayor Claims “Most People Don’t Even Know Where Istria is”
World.content:
September the 17th, 2026 – Dubrovnik Mayor Mato Franković has caused a stir and claimed that “most people don’t even know where Istria is”, adding that “Dubrovnik is the only tourism champion in Croatia”.

Dubrovnik Mayor Mato Franković assessed the tourist season as excellent at a session of the City Council and claimed that Dubrovnik is “the only champion of tourism in Croatia.” Index reports that in his review of the results, which according to him exceed expectations, he directed criticism at the “Istrian lobby,” reports Dubrovački dnevnik.

“The season has been excellent, and what is ahead of us looks very good. So far it looks above expectations,” Franković said.

He also expressed satisfaction that the number of visitors in the historic centre is not exceeding critical levels, after which he sent a message to the competition. “We’re the only champion of tourism in Croatia and no one can measure up to us. Istria with its lobby is trying to present itself as successful. People exclusively from Istria, such as Veljko Ostojić, comment on tourism and they push it. We are alone, but we have shown that we are above everyone,” Franković said, concluding with the statement: “Most people don’t even know where Istria is.”

4.7 million people have come to dubrovnik so far in 2026

On Facebook he was answered by the president of IDS and mayor of Poreč, Loris Peršurić. Peršurić replied to Franković that Dubrovnik is one of the symbols of Croatian tourism and that one should be proud of its successes, but he ironised the claim that people do not know where Istria is.

“Just this year 4.7 million people successfully found it, and we’re only in the 9th month because the season with us lasts almost the whole year,” he wrote. He emphasised that Istria’s reputation was not created overnight, but was built over decades by private renters, owners of agritourism facilities, taverns and wineries, olive growers, caterers, hoteliers, craftsmen and farmers. He also pointed out that in tourism it is not only the numbers that matter, but quality, sustainability and the preservation of space for the people who live in it.

Peršurić added that Dubrovnik also has strong state and tourism tools for promotion at its disposal and concluded that one can be proud of one’s own successes without diminishing those of others. “I therefore invite you to personally convince yourself of the qualities of Istria, but hurry with the reservation because these days quite a few people manage to find us,” he said to Franković.

World.title: Russian Ambassador Summoned for Talks in Croatia Following Russia’s Threats
World.content:
September the 17th, 2026 – The Russian Ambassador has been summoned for talks in Croatia following Russia’s recent threats against various European countries.

Russian Ambassador to Croatia Alexander Nurizade was summoned today for talks at the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs, where the Croatian side expressed concern over security threats from Russia towards European countries, the Russian Embassy in Zagreb announced. Index reports that according to the Russian side, Croatian representatives mentioned incidents in the airspace, territorial waters and on the infrastructure of EU member states, including in Denmark, Lithuania, Romania and Germany. The Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs lists Nurizade on its official website as the current Russian ambassador to Croatia.

the russian ambassador has rejected all accusations

The Russian Embassy states that Nurizade “firmly rejected” the accusations as unfounded. He described them, according to the embassy’s statement, as a “coordinated provocation” aimed at further worsening relations with Russia. He also expressed regret that Croatia, as the Russian side claims, “is pandering to the Kyiv regime and its foreign patrons interested in the continuation of the conflict.” These are the claims of the Russian Embassy. During the talks, Nurizade also repeated the official Russian positions on the causes of the war in Ukraine and accused the West of turning Ukraine into an “anti-Russian project.”

an attempted leipzig drone attack was discussed

Among the cases that the Croatian side, according to the Russian Embassy, cited was the incident in Leipzig. At the beginning of September, the German government officially accused Russia of being behind an attempted drone attack on Leipzig/Halle Airport on 4 August. A drone with explosives was found near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo plane. Berlin claims that the investigation traces the point to the Russian state, while Moscow rejects responsibility. After that case, the European Union and several member states summoned Russian diplomatic representatives for talks. EU High Representative Kaja Kallas said at the time that the incident had the characteristics of state-sponsored terrorism, while Russia claimed that Germany had not provided evidence for its accusations.

a russian vessel fired signal rockets at a danish aircraft

Tensions rose further this week after an incident out in the Baltic Sea. The Danish military announced that a Russian frigate, during routine surveillance, fired two signal rockets at a Danish military Fennec helicopter. One passed at a short distance from the helicopter. Denmark therefore summoned the Russian ambassador for talks. The Russian side countered with an accusation that Danish military helicopters had performed dangerous manoeuvres near Russian warships.

nato had to shoot down a drone over lithuania

In Lithuania a couple of days ago, an Italian fighter jet as part of a NATO mission shot down a drone that had entered Lithuanian airspace from Belarus. Lithuanian authorities announced that the drone was carrying explosives. Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto said it “most likely” came from Russia, but Lithuanian authorities warned that the investigation into its origin is still ongoing and that a final conclusion has not yet been reached. A similar incident was recorded last week in Romania, where a drone that Romanian and Moldovan authorities linked to Russian attacks on Ukraine entered deep into Romanian airspace before returning towards Moldova.

The Russian ambassador in the talks in Zagreb, according to a statement from his embassy, also spoke about Russian attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure. He conveyed that Moscow considers railway junctions, trains and other facilities in Ukraine used for the transport of the army or cargo intended for the Ukrainian armed forces to be “legitimate military targets.”

In recent days Russia has further intensified attacks on Ukrainian railway infrastructure, including areas near the border with NATO members. Ukrainian authorities claim that civilian trains and infrastructure have also been hit in the process. The summoning of Nurizade for talks comes at a time of heightened warnings from European and NATO officials about incidents involving drones, sabotage and other hybrid threats. The European Commission today also proposed a new mechanism for a coordinated response by EU members to such security incidents. An inquiry was also sent to the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs about today’s talks with the Russian ambassador. We asked for confirmation of the meeting, the specific reason for his summoning, and clarification of which incidents Croatia cited and whether it plans further diplomatic steps after the talks.

World.title: Croatia to Get a New Road Worth Over €200 Million
World.content:
September the 17th, 2026 – Croatia is set to get a new road worth over €200 million, and it’s being widely compared to Pelješac Bridge.

The project includes two interchanges, five viaducts, four overpasses and two bridges. Poslovni reports that the Chinese company China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC) is building a 16-kilometre expressway that will finally directly connect Požega with the A3 Zagreb – Lipovac motorway. The new road will link Požeški Brestovac with the Godinjak interchange, where it will then connect to the motorway.

This is one of the largest infrastructure projects in Slavonia, which should significantly improve the transport connectivity of Požega-Slavonia County with the rest of Croatia. The route of the expressway runs south of Daranovci, after which it enters the forested area of Babja gora. There, a single-tube tunnel 1,650 metres long will be built, and the route then descends along a natural valley towards Tisovac and Godinjak. The project includes two interchanges, five viaducts, four overpasses and two bridges. The construction deadline is 48 months, meaning the new road should be completed by the end of 2029.

požega will get a faster link towards both zagreb and slavonski brod

The expressway is being built along the route of the existing state road D51, which has so far been the main transport link between Požega and surrounding settlements with the rest of the country. The new road should bring a safer and higher-quality connection to the A3 motorway, and thereby also to Zagreb and Slavonski Brod.

“This expressway represents the largest single project of Croatian Roads after the Pelješac Bridge. This is a big day not only for Croatian road construction, but also for Požega-Slavonia County, because it will be better and more safely connected to the motorway,” said Transport Minister Oleg Butković at the ceremonial introduction of the contractor into the works in Godinjak in November last year. For the residents of Požega-Slavonia County, the project represents the end of long-standing transport isolation. Due to frequent landslides and damage, the D51 does not fully meet modern standards of safety and traffic flow, so the new expressway will take over an important share of the traffic.

the požega interchange on the A3 motorway is also being built

At the beginning of February, a contract was also signed for the construction of the Požega interchange on the A3 motorway. The Požega interchange is part of the integral project for the construction of the expressway, which will connect to the motorway precisely at that point. The investor for that part of the project is Croatian Roads. When the works are completed, after decades of waiting Požega will finally get a direct fast road link with the A3 motorway, which should further improve the transport accessibility of the city and the entire Požega-Slavonia County.

World.title: US redirects millions in security assistance away from Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US State Department notified Congress on Tuesday that it is redirecting $52 million in foreign military financing away from Tunisia, Iraq, Slovakia, and North Macedonia.

“Thank you, President Trump and Secretary Rubio, for redirecting millions in security assistance away from Tunisia and Iraq and providing it instead to our partners in this hemisphere,” US Representative Joe Wilson said in a statement on X.

According to statements from the US Department of State, the funds are being reallocated to Panama, Peru, Ecuador, and Colombia.

The funds would battle drug-related terrorism, help safeguard the Panama Canal, and prevent foreign enemies from gaining strategic footholds in the Western Hemisphere, according to the US State Department.

The change followed Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s visit to Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru, during which he affirmed a strategy prioritizing the Western Hemisphere to secure borders, control immigration, and combat organized crime.

The shift results in a reduction of security aid for Tunisia, Iraq, Slovakia, and North Macedonia, although it does not entirely eliminate funding for these countries. The specific amount of remaining funds allocated to them has not been disclosed.

World.title: Iraq appoints new ambassador to US
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s new Ambassador to the United States, Krikor Der-Hagopian, officially presented his credentials to US President Donald Trump on Tuesday during a formal ceremony at the White House.

According to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry, Ambassador Der-Hagopian’s mission aims to keep track of the outcomes of Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s visit to the United States, working to build a new chapter in Iraqi-American relations, broadening strategic ties, and expanding political, economic, investment, and security cooperation to strengthen Iraq’s regional role and serve the interests of both countries.

Der-Hagopian will work on advancing the economic, investment, energy, and security memoranda of understanding established during al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington in July.

The appointment of the new ambassador marks an important shift in Baghdad’s diplomatic strategy. As an Armenian Christian, Der-Hagopian is the first non-Shiite envoy sent by Iraq to Washington in modern history.

Der-Hagopian was educated in Denver, Colorado, and has prior experience working with former President Barham Saleh and former Prime Minister Mohamed Shia al-Sudani.

Foreign policy analysts see Der-Hagopian’s selection as a clear indication that Iraq is prioritizing highly skilled, strategic trust-builders to handle Baghdad’s relationship with Washington.

Der-Hagopian follows diplomat Nizar al-Khairallah, who has held the position since June 2023.

World.title: Iraq stores oil in facility in Kirkuk to raise exports via Turkey’s Ceyhan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has initiated a trial operation to transport crude oil using tanker trucks from its southern oil fields to a storage facility in Kirkuk, an effort that aims to enhance oil supplies destined for the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

This initiative is part of a broader Iraqi effort to increase oil flows through the northern export route after the US-Israeli war against Iran disrupted Iraqi shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, the country’s main export channel.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, said that the ministry has reached a deal with Iraq-based KAR Group to transport crude oil using its fleet of tanker trucks. This arrangement was confirmed in a statement issued by the state-owned Basra Oil Company (BOC).

BOC stated that the trial operation began on September 13 and lasted two days, during which slightly over six million liters of crude oil, equivalent to about 38,000 barrels, were transported on 209 tanker trucks, each with a capacity of 30,000 liters.

According to Oil Ministry estimates, current oil flows from northern Iraq to the Turkish port of Ceyhan are believed to be around 200,000 barrels per day, a decrease from roughly 250,000 before the Iran conflict.

According to BOC sources, the project faces logistical obstacles such as a shortage of tanker trucks and inadequate loading facilities in the southern oil fields. The initial volumes remain too small to allow for a significant increase in exports from north Iraq.

World.title: EBRD boosts trade financing in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is bolstering trade financing in Iraq by extending a credit ceiling of up to US$ 25 million (€21.3 million) to Bank of Baghdad, one of Iraq’s main private-sector banks.

The initiative is part of the EBRD’s Trade Facilitation Program (TFP) and aims to assist the Bank of Baghdad in enhancing its import and export transactions, as well as expanding its correspondent banking relationships.

The funding will assist in closing trade financing gaps in Iraq, improve access to trade finance for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) involved in cross-border trade, and boost commercial ties with regional and worldwide markets.

The technical cooperation funded by the EBRD will include advising help, specialized training, access to the EBRD Trade Finance e-Learning Program, and seminars on essential trade finance subjects.

The European Union will fund the creation of a dedicated training curriculum for the Bank of Baghdad, focusing on core and advanced banking competencies, improving staff skills, strengthening service delivery, and promoting the continued development of Iraq’s banking sector.

The initiative will also promote financial inclusion by providing a specific training module on increasing access to financial services for underrepresented populations, particularly women.

The Bank of Baghdad is one of Iraq’s top three private banks, with total assets of $2.2 billion by the end of 2025 and 35 branches around the nation.

In 1999, the EBRD launched the TFP initiative to enhance international commerce. The program provides guarantees and short-term loans to selected participating banks, which in turn support local exporters, importers, and distributors.

World.title: Iraq, Turkey finalize draft transport infrastructure agreement
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Transport Ministry announced on Friday that Iraq and Turkey have finalized an agreement regarding the development of transport infrastructure.

The agreement paves the way for official government recognition and a formal signature.

The deal was reached after a memorandum of understanding was reached by Iraqi Transport Minister Wahab al-Hassani and Turkish Transport and Infrastructure Minister Abdulkadir Uraloglu in late July.

Officials from both sides completed the document after four days of intense discussions in Baghdad.

The agreement formulates a comprehensive institutional framework to regulate cooperation in developing infrastructure projects and modernizing transportation systems.

The draft framework includes a program to implement various phases of the Development Road, a strategic project proposed by Iraq to transport goods and energy from Basra to Turkey, in accordance with the approved technical priorities, timelines, and project completion requirements.

Given the economic and developmental importance of the Development Road project to Iraq and the region, this step serves as a critical foundation for consolidating Iraqi-Turkish cooperation and organizing joint working mechanisms.

The move is part of Iraq’s efforts to upgrade the transport sector and boost investment opportunities and economic integration, supporting strategic projects and strengthening Iraq’s position as a key hub for transport, trade, and regional and international supply chains.

World.title: Where the US-China tariff row stands ahead of White House summit
World.content:
Beijing – Trade frictions between the world’s top two economies are set to take centre stage next week when US President Donald Trump hosts Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping at the White House.

Although a shaky truce was reached last October that halted the frenzied escalating tariff battle launched by Trump, a comprehensive and permanent deal has remained elusive.

Here is where things stand ahead of the summit, which is expected to take place on September 24:

How high are current levies?

Tariffs have represented a major hurdle in the China-US trade relationship since 2018, during Trump’s first term.

In April 2025, the base US tariff rate on Chinese goods reached an eye-watering 145 percent — matched by China’s reciprocal levies of 125 percent — although both sides have since significantly reduced rates.

Tolls are now imposed by both sides in a complex patchwork of sector-specific policies.

The effective tariff rate for imports from China, which balances various duties paid across all items, was 22.8 percent as of July, the highest among all major US trading partners, according to research organisation the Penn Wharton Budget Model.

Among the highest effective tariff rates for Chinese goods heading to the United States are 40.5 percent on steel and aluminium, it said.

China still maintains a 10 percent levy on all US goods, with additional rates applicable in other specific sectors, such as 15 percent on liquid natural gas.

How much is still being traded?

Trade between the world’s two largest economies has continued despite the turbulence caused by the tariffs.

Total imports and exports hit $400.8 billion in January through August this year, Chinese customs data shows, a 5.4 percent rise from the same period in 2025.

But the balance is lopsided, with Chinese exports accounting for 75 percent of that.

Beijing’s soaring trade surplus has long ruffled feathers in Washington, while a similar asymmetry with the European Union is also exacerbating tensions with Brussels.

What is being discussed?

Trump told reporters on Sunday that he would be discussing “almost everything” with Xi at the summit.

Tariffs, however, are “the main issue on the agenda”, Dan Wang, a director on Eurasia Group’s China team, told AFP. “Xi wouldn’t go if there were no deliverables on tariffs or a trade truce,” she said.

Beijing and Washington are currently in consultation about a tariff reduction framework covering $30 billion worth of products on each side, China’s commerce ministry said last week.

That goal was agreed at Xi’s last meeting with Trump in Beijing in May, during which they also agreed to establish trade and investment councils intended to manage friction.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday that he will meet his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng this weekend for talks expected to lay the groundwork for the White House summit.

What is China’s leverage?

Beijing successfully pressured Washington to back down from its sky-high tariffs last year after imposing stringent controls on exports of rare earths, the critical minerals used for various high-tech products whose processing is dominated by China.

“China still has the upper hand” going into next week’s talks, said Wang of Eurasia Group.

The country’s supply chains are “very flexible”, and its historic boom in exports has not been significantly dented by tariffs so far, she noted.

Xi’s diplomatic clout has also been on full display recently, having met this month with several leaders including Russian President Vladimir Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, traveling to Bishkek, Cairo and New Delhi.

What is Trump seeking?

With global oil prices spiking following renewed fighting in the US war with Iran, the Trump administration is looking to allay concerns about the economy ahead of crucial midterm elections in November.

Securing Chinese guarantees to purchase US agricultural goods, particularly soybeans, has been a recurring objective in trade talks with Beijing.

The meeting will also give Trump the chance to project statesmanship while hosting a high-stakes diplomatic engagement at the White House — Xi’s first visit to the US capital in 11 years.

What are other potential pitfalls?

Several other fraught issues threaten to derail any sweeping agreement.

Beijing’s economic and diplomatic support for Tehran is one major sticking point, with recent reports by the Wall Street Journal claiming that Chinese entities supplied Iran with satellite imagery of a military base housing US troops in Jordan.

Fierce technological competition is also ongoing, particularly in the closely watched artificial intelligence sector.

The US government last week accused Chinese AI labs of stealing the capabilities of US firms on an “industrial scale”.

World.title: Most stocks rise as Fed hikes and indicates drive to curb inflation
World.content:
Hong Kong – Most equities rose Thursday after the Federal Reserve hiked interest rates for the first time in three years and boss Kevin Warsh sounded a hawkish note that ramped up bets on another increase as officials fight surging inflation.

Investor sentiment was also given a lift by hopes for a pick-up in oil supplies from Saudi Arabia after the country moved to restore some capacity from a pipeline it closed at the weekend following drone attacks.

In a unanimous decision, the Fed lifted borrowing costs for the first time since 2023, defying President Donald Trump’s demand for cuts, as Warsh stressed the need to combat inflation that has been “too high” for “too long”.

“We removed a dose of accommodation so that financial and credit conditions would be more consistent with our ultimate objectives,” Warsh said after the announcement.

“Today’s action starts to show we’re serious about this, and we will deliver on the price stability objective.”

The decision was announced along with a graph showing the vast majority of Fed policymakers saw at least one more was likely necessary before the end of the year.

Traders now see an October hike as being a 50:50.

While Wall Street’s three main indexes ended Wednesday in the red, Asian traders took the 25-basis-point lift more positively, with analysts saying it shored up credibility in the central bank and provided some reassurance over officials’ determination to beat inflation.

Long-term government bond yields — which this week touched two-decade highs — fell as investors pared back their inflation expectations, which at 3.4 percent is currently well above the bank’s two percent target.

“Removing a dose of accommodation is not the language of a central bank that believes it has completed the job,” said Stephen Innes at Quintex Intel.

“It suggests policy was still providing support before Wednesday and may not yet be restrictive after it.

“The hike removed the immediate credibility question. The explanation created a new argument about how much tightening remains.”

And Christian Scherrmann at DWS added: “Overall, we believe the main motivation this time was credibility, given bond market pricing and recent developments in oil markets.”

Still, he added: “Despite his hawkish stance, Fed Chair Warsh’s optimistic outlook on the economy may be music to many ears.”

Equity markets across Asia were mostly higher in early trade.

Tokyo, Seoul, Singapore, Taipei, Wellington and Jakarta all advanced, though Hong Kong and Shanghai dipped.

However, Tai Hui, of JP Morgan Asset Management, warned: “We think the chance of U.S. policy rates returning to above five percent is still limited.

“Nonetheless, a catalyst to extend the equity bull market (lower interest rates) is looking unlikely in the foreseeable future.”

The news angered Trump, who called Warsh a “good man” who had “a hostile board”.

“They’re raising the rates to make Trump do as bad as they can possibly do… So they’re raising that only for political reasons, and that’s a raise against Trump,” he complained.

While the Middle East crisis continues to weigh heavily on sentiment and oil prices above $100 a barrel, investors took some cheer from reports that Saudi Arabia is looking to return about half the capacity of its cross-country oil pipeline within days.

The East-West conduit was shut last week after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis targeted it.

State-run Saudi Aramco said it was looking to get back up to full capacity in about six weeks, Bloomberg cited sources as saying.

The news sent crude prices tumbling around three percent Wednesday, and they extended the losses Thursday.

The Fed hike and Warsh’s remarks also pushed the dollar higher against its peers and held the gains in early trade.

Eyes are now on decisions by the central banks of Britain and Japan, with the latter also expected to hike as it looks to fend off a rise in inflation and a weaker yen.

World.title: US again denies Palestinian leader Abbas visa to attend UN assembly
World.content:
Washington – The United States has denied Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas an entry visa to attend the UN General Assembly in New York next week, a source familiar with the case said Wednesday.

In a separate statement that did not mention Abbas by name, the State Department say it would deny visas to members of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) and officials with the Palestinian Authority (PA), “as a consequence of their failure to reform, contrary to their commitments to the United States, and their ongoing activities that undermine the prospects for peace.”

A source familiar with the matter confirmed to AFP that the Palestinian Authority president, Abbas, was covered by the measure.

The Trump administration took the same step last year, forcing the Palestinian leader, a regular at the UN General Assembly, to address the body of global leadership by video.

In its statement Wednesday, the State Department said that the PLO and PA had “once again, failed to live up to their commitments.”

“This includes initiating and supporting actions at international organizations that undermine and contradict prior commitments,” the department also said.

Washington also accused the organizations of “taking actions to internationalize the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict including through the International Criminal Court (ICC) and International Court of Justice (ICJ), seeking to bypass negotiations through seeking unilateral recognition, and continuing to pay stipends to terrorists and to glorify acts of terrorism and terrorists in public pronouncements and school textbooks.”

The move puts the United States at odds with numerous countries, including France, that recognized a Palestinian state at the United Nations last year.

A total of 142 UN member states endorsed it following the conference on a two-state solution co-chaired by France and Saudi Arabia.

The decision comes as violence by Israeli settlers against Palestinians has escalated in recent months in the West Bank.

Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967, and violence there has surged since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack that triggered the war in the Gaza Strip.

According to an AFP tally based on Palestinian health ministry data, Israeli soldiers or settlers have killed at least 1,109 Palestinians in the West Bank — fighters and civilians — since October 7, 2023, when a Hamas-led attack killed more than 1,200 people.

The ensuing Israeli military campaign waged relentless strikes on Gaza that have killed more than 73,700 people, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

The international community has expressed concern over the violence, but the United States has remained largely quiet on the issue, saying only that the US government opposes any annexation of Palestinian territory.

World.title: 'BJP and EC join forces to split party': Rahul Gandhi slams EC over TMC name, symbol freeze
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition

on Friday slammed the

for barring TMC from using party name and symbol in the upcoming assembly bypolls in West Bengal, accusing the poll panel and

of joining forces to split a party.

In a social media post on X, Rahul pointed towards the past examples of split in shiv Sena and NCP.

"First Shiv Sena, then NCP, and now

Trinamool Congress

. Every time, the same patternâBJP and the Election Commission join forces to split a party. Then its election symbol is snatched away," the Congress leader said.

"When an entire party can be stolen, it's hardly surprising that the votes of millions of Indians can be stolen too," he added.

Rahul also said that "vote chori, sarkaar chori and now party chori have become the symbols of democratic decline" in the country.

"Vote theft. Government theft. Now party theftâthese have become symbols of our democratic decline. The ECI's constitutional responsibility is to protect the mandateâbut instead, it's aiding those very forces that overturn the people's verdict," the Congress leader said.

"This fight isn't just Mamata Banerjee's. It's the fight of every political party, every voter who wants free and fair elections," he added.





Rahul's remarks came after the poll panel, in its interim order, ruled that neither faction of TMC can use its name or "flowers and grass" symbol after acknowledging a split between factions led by Mamata Banerjee and Arup Roy.

Both groups will have to contest the bypolls under different names and with election symbols allotted by the Commission. This arrangement will continue until the dispute is finally settled.

EC said two rival groups each claimed to be the "real" party, requiring substantive determination under Paragraph 15 of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968. It said the interim measure, based on precedents, would place them on an "even keel".

Meanwhile, West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh claimed that TMC is crumbling under the weight of severe internal strife following the Election Commission's interim order.

"The Trinamool Congress (TMC) is disintegrating due to internal infighting. The public has rejected them. Their MPs are in other parties, and Mamata Banerjee stands alone. They hold no documents regarding this; the Election Commission will make the decision," he said.

The dispute reached the Election Commission in July after the rival factions staked competing claims to control of the TMC. The panel subsequently sought responses on issues including organisational control, authorised signatories, party assets, name and election symbol.

World.title: Air India Express suspends 8 crew members for missing post-flight declaration deadline
World.content:

NEW DELHI: Air India Express suspended eight crew members for three months for failing to complete the mandatory post-flight declaration, news agency ANI reported, citing sources.The incident took place on August 2 after the flight landed in Amritsar from Dubai.According to ANI, the crew was required to undergo the post-flight declaration within two hours of landing. However, they were delayed by 35 minutes and submitted the declaration after two hours and 35 minutes."As per the airlineâs mandatory rules for testing of psychoactive substances, all crew members underwent the test, and the reports came negative," sources told ANI."The entire incident was reported to the DGCA, and the airline decided to suspend the eight crew members for three months," they added.According to DGCA rules, crew members operating international flights for Indian carriers must complete a post-flight alcohol test within two hours of landing in India, regardless of individual circumstances during that window.

World.title: SC takes exception to 31 unnatural deaths in Manipur relief camps
World.content:
The bench directed the state chief secretary to submit what remedial measures would be taken to prevent such incidents

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday took strong exception to 31 unnatural deaths in Manipur's relief camps - set up after the eruption of Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes in 2023 to shelter internally displaced persons (IDPs) - including one due to sexual assault.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the state govt to file an affidavit giving details of the causes of death as ascertained through postmortem reports and the investigations to identify the culprits. It also questioned the state for giving a meagre Rs 30,000 as compensation to the next of kin even though the state had paid Rs 4 lakh-5 lakh to relatives of victims of the ethnic clashes.This order was passed after perusing Justice Gita Mittal Committee's report. Placed before the court by senior advocate Vibha D Makhija, it cited a TOI report of June 7 which published a news report on 731 deaths, including 25 unnatural deaths, in relief camps as disclosed by the state home department. TOI had also reported that 43,000 IDPs were residing in various relief camps.Makhija said when the committee sought details of the deaths, the state initially provided sketchy statistics.Only after prodding did govt provide the required information. Jiribam and Churachandpur relief camps recorded nine unnatural deaths each; six were reported in Bishnupur, four in Imphal West, two in Imphal East and one in Kakching.The bench directed the state chief secretary to submit what remedial measures would be taken to prevent such incidents. It also asked the state to detail the steps taken to expedite investigations into the FIRs.Justice Mittal Committee informed the court that the mother of the sexual assault victim in Churachandpur relief camp was given Rs 2.5 lakh as compensation but in most cases, the next of kin got only Rs 30,000. In Kangpokpi relief camp, where 128 IDPs died natural deaths, no compensation was paid to their kin, it said.

World.title: Centre agrees to lower cut-off for NEET-SS admission
World.content:
SC last week asked govt to reconsider its decision not to reduce the cut-off percentile

NEW DELHI: Nudged by Supreme Court to reduce the cut-off percentile for admission to super specialty medical courses to fill around 2,000 vacant seats, Centre Thursday told the court that the qualifying percentile for NEET-SS may go from the existing 50th to 30th for the proposed special stray vacancy round, to be conducted soon, reports Amit Anand Choudhary.SC last week asked govt to reconsider its decision not to reduce the cut-off percentile in order to ensure seats were not wasted. Govt filed a two-page note before a bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe and said "the matter has since been reconsidered in consultation with stakeholders concerned"."In order to ensure available super specialty seats do not remain vacant and that the available training capacity is optimally utilised, it has been decided that the qualifying percentile for NEET-SS may be reduced from existing 50th percentile to 30th percentile for the purpose of proposed special stray vacancy round," govt said.It, however, told SC those students who had already taken admission would not be allowed to participate in the special stray vacancy round. It proposed the round "be conducted strictly in accordance with the existing principles or rules applicable to a stray vacancy round, with no provision for upgradation of candidates who are already holding/joined a seat", govt said.After the second round of NEET-SS counselling, 1,857 super specialty seats - including 1,094 DM/MCh seats and 763 DNB-SS seats - were vacant. A substantial number of these pertain to highly specialised medical and surgical disciplines.

World.title: Tamil Nadu must change mindset, allow Hindi in schools: SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday told Tamil Nadu govt that it needed to change its mindset towards teaching Hindi in schools and should thrash out issues with Centre on setting up Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district.

As Vijay-led TN govt took the same stand taken by the previous DMK govt, a bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and A G Masih said individual states could not act like countries. "You have to change your mindset, it can't be that Hindi will not be taught on the soil of TN," the bench said.

TN has been opposing the setting up of these schools as they follow a three-language policy, including Hindi, which is against the state's two-language policy.

"We are saying in addition to all the good things you're doing in your state, having something in addition will not bring down your standards... People in Chennai should not alienate Delhi and vice versa," SC said.

Senior advocate Jaideep Gupta, appearing for the state, submitted it was against the federal structure to impose Centre's decision on a state. "It is against the state policy. It supersedes Tamil. This kind of unification is not the purport of Constitution.





It is not a central govt school. It is a school run by a society. There is an adamancy that Hindi must predominate," he said.

Gupta submitted that cooperative federalism would never work in only one direction and such a policy should not be enforced by the court.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The bench asked the state to comply with its order and posted the case for further hearing in Dec. SC had last Dec directed TN to identify land required for establishing Navodaya Vidyalayas in each district within six weeks.

"We are not asking you to acquire land. We are only asking you to identify it... There is a need for dialogue. You can't say I won't accept a policy. Today it is education, tomorrow it will be something else. You have to relax this rigidity in your mind," SC said.

The court was hearing TN's plea challenging a Madras HC judgement directing it to set up Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district. HC had ruled that Navodaya Vidyalayas did not violate Tamil Nadu Tamil Learning Act and the state's blanket refusal to set up such schools curtailed students' right to choose educational institutions.

World.title: BJP must light a diya to atone for its sins: Congress
World.content:
Kharge and Rahul Gandhi targeted BJP over âmalgovernanceâ and âlighting of diyasâ

New Delhi: Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi targeted BJP over "malgovernance" and "lighting of diyas" during its lamp-lighting campaign for PM Narendra Modi's birthday."In Balaghat, more than 30 tribal children have died amid illness, malnutrition and a lack of basic health facilities. The extent of the callousness is such that innocent lives kept slipping away, yet the response remained sluggish, and the govt kept sleeping," Rahul told MP CM Mohan Yadav."Chief minister, if you have found time after lighting lamps and holding celebrations, take a look at the ground reality in the state," he said, while citing spurious medicines and hooch deaths.Kharge cited Maharashtra govt findings of healthcare markups exceeding 2,000%, saying, "on World Patient Safety Day, Modi govt stands exposed for turning patients into prey. Hospitals are charging a staggering 2,841% markup on basic medical consumables like IVs, according to the Maharashtra FDA, exposing the brazen robbery of common patients, especially in private hospitals."He added, "food, retail and wholesale inflation are already very high and burning the pockets of common people. Perhaps, the BJP should light a diya to atone for its pathetic misgovernance and sins."

World.title: SC slams builders for anonymous complaints against judges
World.content:
We will direct a CBI inquiry into these complaints to find out who are behind it,â said bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant &d Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday took a serious view of a large number of anonymous complaints received by it against judges, amici curiae and counsel after SC turned up the heat on several realtors and builders for misusing subvention schemes, duping homebuyers, delaying projects and refusing to refund the money invested."We will direct a CBI inquiry into these complaints to find out who are behind it," said a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, after additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati handed over the CBI status report on its investigations into builders who had misused subvention schemes in collusion with bank officials, resulting in homebuyers paying EMIs without any hope of getting their dream homes even after waiting for decades.CJI Kant asked, "In these matters, who are the counsel representing the builders? You (builders) have started sending anonymous complaints to us? You people do not know what kind of stubborn people we are."Turning to Bhati, the CJI said on the next hearing date, "we will give you another set of complaints. You inquire into them and find out who the people responsible for writing these are. Most of them will be builders, we assume, and, of course, some counsel who have ill-advised them"."We will catch hold of them. Do you think we will get cowed down by this? We will direct CBI to register an FIR and investigate them. We will take it to the logical conclusion," the bench said.In April last year, SC had ordered a CBI investigation into the abuse of subvention agreements by builders and banks. At the last hearing, Bhati had informed SC that CBI had registered 50 FIRs and completed probes in 18 of them, filing 17 chargesheets and a closure report before competent courts.She said several bank officials were found to have been in collusion with the builders and were named among the accused in the chargesheets, and the agency had invoked provisions of Prevention of Corruption Act against them. CBI has sought sanctions for prosecuting bank officials from State Bank of India, Bank of India, Uco Bank, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank.SC had directed banks to expeditiously grant sanction for prosecution and said failure to do so would warrant submission of an explanation before the court.SC had also directed CBI to conduct a thorough investigation into allegations of misrepresentation and other irregularities by entities known as "Ozone group in Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu; Vivansaa in Bengaluru; Rudra Buildwell Pvt Ltd in Greater Noida; and Omaxe group in Chandigarh". It had sought a separate probe status report in this regard.

World.title: Early voting begins in U.S. midterm elections that could flip control of Congress
World.content:
In-person voting for this year's midterm elections begins on Friday (September 18, 2026), ushering in the final six weeks for Americans to decide who they trust to lead Congress through a cost-of-living crisis, a prolonged war in Iran, and other pressing issues.

Election administrators say they're prepared and confident the vote will be accurate and secure. Nevertheless, President Donald Trump has continued with efforts to denigrate certain voting methods and reshape how U.S. elections are run, through court challenges, an expansive federal hunt for non-citizen voters and a pressure campaign to force election officials to share sensitive voter data.

Friday (September 18, 2026) marks the start of early voting in Virginia. Voters in a handful of other states, including Idaho, Minnesota and South Dakota, are able to cast absentee ballots in person, typically at a local election office or voting centre. More expansive early voting is scheduled to begin in those and other states in the coming weeks.

The November 3 election includes votes for governor and state legislature in most states and will determine whether the U.S. House and Senate maintain their Republican majorities.

If Democrats retake Congress, it will alter the trajectory of the final two years of Mr. Trump's term, likely leading to investigations and other oversight efforts.

The start of early voting comes at a time of deep angst among many Americans about issues including rising gas and grocery prices, the war in Iran, the looming risks of artificial intelligence technology, and Mr. Trump's aggressive immigration enforcement campaign.

It also follows an unprecedented spate of mid-decade redistricting for the U.S. House that began when Mr. Trump urged the Republican-controlled legislature in Texas to redraw its congressional map to help the party. California and other states followed.

The changes affect millions of people: Research shows 1 in 10 Americans this fall are residents of a different congressional district than in 2024.

Those partisan efforts are expected to continue ahead of the 2028 elections after a landmark ruling earlier this year from the Supreme Court weakened the federal Voting Rights Act's protections against racially discriminatory redistricting.

As the start of early voting approached, Mr. Trump was focused on efforts to assert federal control over election administration, even as the Constitution bestows the power to run elections on the states and, in some cases, Congress.

The Supreme Court rejected Mr. Trump's bid to restrict mail ballots this week, but several of his administration's other efforts to influence the voting process and mine state voter lists for illegitimate voters are ongoing.

Mr. Trump for years has raised the spectre of widespread non-citizen voting in U.S. elections, and this year is no exception. But despite his administration's insistence that hundreds of thousands of people are illegally on voting rolls across the country, research continues to show noncitizen voting is exceptionally rare.

David Becker, executive director and founder of the Center for Election Innovation and Research, said he wouldn't be surprised if the president continues “his disinformation campaign and his attack on election officials”. But he said he thinks despite that and other challenges, “ultimately the process will hold as it has in past years”. Voting rights advocates have encouraged voters this year to cast mail ballots early, in part because of concerns about recent changes in U.S. Postal Service operations that could delay the application of postmarks to ballots.

“Voting early, whether in person or by mail, is good for all of our communities because it gives voters options, eases lines on Election Day and can even mean faster results,” said Hannah Fried, co-founder and CEO of the voting rights group All Voting Is Local.

In a press briefing on Thursday (September 17, 2026), Minnesota Secretary of State Steve Simon urged people not to be swayed by stories they might have seen or read that cast doubt on election operations. They would be able to vote “just like they always have”, he said.

“I just want to reaffirm that Minnesota's elections are fundamentally free, fair, accurate, honest and secure,” he said.

World.title: Congress government engages in politics concerning people’s lives, not their sentiments, says Karnataka CM
World.content:
Karnataka’s Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar said that the Congress government engages in politics concerning people’s lives, not their sentiments.

“Our government will work in alignment with everyone’s aspirations,” he told press persons at the Circuit House in Mangaluru ahead of the 21st Cabinet meeting scheduled in the city on September 18.

“For us, people’s lives are more important than politics. Leaders from any party need not be alarmed,” he said. “I visited the house where Mahatma Gandhi had stayed and had breakfast. I enjoyed Mangaluru buns and dosa. I will go wherever the district minister takes me,” he said.

The Chief Minister interacted with social media influencers at a popular restaurant over breakfast.

Seventeen (17) subjects have been listed on the agenda for discussion at the Cabinet meeting.

Mr. Shivakumar and his ministerial colleagues are expected to travel together to the Cabinet meeting at Praja Soudha in an open top bus, according to Dakshina Kannada district in-charge Minister U. T. Khader.

The ministers are expected to converge at the Kadri Manjunatha temple in the morning before commencing their journey to the district office complex, Praja Soudha, at Padil. The ministers would board an open top double decker bus of Karnataka State Tourism Development Corporation (KSTDC) around 10 a.m. They will travel in the bus from Bhagwan Mahaveer (Pumpwell) Circle to Praja Soudha.

World.title: Police debunk ‘24-karat gold-plated’ Ganesh idol claims in Hyderabad’s Goshamahal
World.content:
Claims circulating on social media that the ‘Lee Chee Ka Raja Ganesh – 2026’ idol in Goshamahal, Hyderabad, was made of Panchaloha, plated with 24-karat gold and studded with nearly 3.84 lakh American diamonds are false and misleading, Goshamahal police said on Thursday (September 17, 2026).

The clarification came after photographs, videos and messages about the idol were widely shared on social media. The posts claimed that the idol weighed around 48 kg, was crafted from five metals, had a 24-karat gold-plated finish and was studded with 3,83,800 American diamonds.

The police said the idol was not made using the materials or in the manner claimed in the posts. They particularly rejected the repeatedly circulated claim that it had been plated with 24-karat gold.

According to police, some committee members and organisers associated with ‘Lee Chee Ka Raja Ganesh’ were allegedly involved in publicising the claims. The police alleged that the publicity was intended to promote the commercial interests of Lee Chee Pearls and Jewels and obtain wrongful gain by creating a false impression about the idol among the public.

The police said exaggerated and unverified claims about the idol’s composition and value could mislead people and generate unnecessary attention and confusion.

Public has been asked not to believe or forward unverified claims about the idol on WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram, X or other social media platforms. The police specifically cautioned users against circulating claims concerning the purported gold plating, panchaloha composition, weight and number of diamonds used.

Goshamahal Police Inspector B. Sravan Kumar urged people to rely on verified information and exercise caution before forwarding material on social media. Police also appealed to the public to prevent the spread of false or misleading information during the Ganesh festival.

World.title: Malaysia's King allows former leader Najib to serve rest of his graft sentence under house arrest
World.content:
Malaysia's King on Friday (September 18, 2026) granted jailed former Prime Minister Najib Razak a rare royal clemency, allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison term for graft under house arrest.

The decision came at a suddenly convened Pardons Board meeting, a week after the board deferred Najib's latest clemency application to a future meeting.

It marked an unprecedented use of house arrest as a form of royal clemency in Malaysia and could renew debate over royal powers, the rule of law and the treatment of Malaysia's most prominent corruption convict.

A statement issued by the Legal Affairs Department under the Prime Minister's office said Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar has granted a “conditional pardon” for Najib during a Pardons Board meeting. Najib will be allowed to serve the remainder of his prison term under house arrest until August 23, 2028, if he pays the 50 million ringgit fine ($12 million) imposed by the court, it said.

The statement said Najib must also follow conditions set, failing which the pardon will be forfeited. No details were provided.

Najib, 73, has been imprisoned since August 2022 after Malaysia's top court upheld his conviction in a graft case linked to the multi-billion dollar looting of the state investment fund 1Malaysia Development Berhad.

He was originally sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined 210 million ringgit ($51.5 million) in 2020 for abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving 42 million ringgit ($10.3 million) channelled into his bank accounts from SRC International, a former unit of 1MDB.

In January 2024, a Pardons Board chaired by the then-king halved his sentence to six years and reduced his fine to 50 million ringgit.

Najib has maintained the previous king, Sultan Abdullah Ahmad Shah, also issued an addendum order allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. But the High Court ruled that the alleged house arrest order was not enforceable because it had not been raised or discussed by the Pardons Board at its January 2024 meeting.

The house-arrest order also raises questions about a separate graft sentence for Najib.

In December 2025, Najib was found guilty for abuse of power and money laundering related to over USD 700 million channelled into his bank accounts from 1MDB, in his main trial tied to the fund. He was sentenced to another 15 years in prison and fined 11.4 billion ringgit ($2.8 billion), which is to take effect after his existing sentence ends. He is appealing that conviction.

House arrest had been discussed as part of broader criminal-justice reforms in Malaysia. In 2024, the government said proposed legislation allowing home detention in certain circumstances was aimed at reducing prison overcrowding and recidivism, not designed specifically for Najib.

Najib set up the 1MDB development fund shortly after he took office in 2009. Investigators allege at least USD 4.5 billion was stolen from the fund and laundered by Najib's associates through layers of bank accounts in the US and other countries. The funds were allegedly used to finance Hollywood films and extravagant purchases that included hotels, a luxury yacht, art and jewelry.

A national outrage over the 1MDB scandal led to the historic 2018 election defeat of the party that had governed Malaysia since independence from Britain in 1957.

Despite his conviction, Najib still holds clout in his party, the United Malays National Organisation, which is now part of Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's unity government that took power after the 2022 elections.

World.title: Dharwad tahsildar caught taking ₹50 lakh bribe by Lokayukta
World.content:
The Lokayukta Police arrested Dharwad tahsildar Sachchidanand Kachanur while he was allegedly taking ₹50 lakh as bribe for rectification of records. He was remanded in 14-day judicial custody by the Lokayukta Special Court in Dharwad on September 17.

The Lokayukta sleuths had caught Mr. Kachanur red-handed late at night near Karnatak College in Dharwad on September 16. He was produced in court on September 17. He was remanded to judicial custody till October 1.

According to Lokayukta Police, the official had allegedly demanded ₹1 crore in two instalments of ₹50 lakh each, besides one acre of land, in connection with changes to the title records of a 33-acre plot in Yerikoppa village, located around 12 km from Dharwad on the Pune-Bengaluru National Highway.

The landowner, Manjunath of Bagalkot, allegedly approached the Lokayukta police after the demand was made. Acting on his complaint, the officials registered a case. The Lokayukta police seized ₹50 lakh in cash during the operation.

The Lokayukta Police is investigating the circumstances surrounding the alleged demand, including whether any other persons were involved. The police are also examining documents relating to the mutation and title-transfer process concerning the Yerikoppa property.

Lokayukta officers described the operation as a major one considering the involvement of a serving Revenue Department official and the amount of cash seized. Further investigation is on.

Union Minister alleges involvement of Congress leaders

Speaking to presspersons, Union Minister Pralhad Joshi urged Karnataka’s Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to order a judicial inquiry into the case. He said that he had information that some Congress leaders were present when the cash was being handed over, and alleged that they were sent away from the scene by the sleuths under pressure. He demanded a thorough inquiry into the alleged involvement of Congress leaders in the case.

World.title: Central GST Superintendent caught taking ₹8 lakh bribe in Bengaluru
World.content:
A Central GST (CGST) Superintendent and a private individual were arrested by the Bengaluru City Lokayukta police on September 17 for allegedly demanding and taking a ₹8-lakh bribe to close a complaint against a city-based businessman.

The accused public servant has been identified as Mohit Pratap Singh, Superintendent, CGST, South Division-4, South Commissionerate. The second accused is Salman Sheikh, a private individual who allegedly acted as a mediator in the transaction.

According to the Lokayukta police, the duo allegedly demanded ₹8 lakh from Syed Zameer to close a complaint filed against him in connection with a pending Central GST matter.

Acting on a complaint by Mr. Zameer, the Bengaluru City Lokayukta team caught the duo taking the bribe in the chamber of the Superintendent in the Kendriya Sadan at Koramangala.

The Lokayukta police subsequently arrested the two accused. A case was registered under Section 7A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

World.title: Visually challenged students write exams without help of scribes at Andhra Loyola College
World.content:
Nine visually challenged students studying first-year degree course in Andhra Loyola College (ALC) wrote their first mid-semester examinations without the help of scribes on Thursday.

The students keyed in their answers on laptops, after which the answer scripts were printed and forwarded to the respective examiners for evaluation.

College Principal Fr. Melchior said the initiative reflects ALC’s commitment to inclusive education and the use of accessible technology to empower students with disabilities.

Correspondent Fr. Francis Xavier described the initiative as an important step towards helping visually challenged students become confident and independent learners.

With this, 16 of the 36 visually challenged students enrolled across the Intermediate and Degree programmes at ALC are now able to write examinations independently using laptops.

Professor of Physics and Coordinator of the Higher Education and Persons with Special Needs (HEPSN) initiative G. Sahaya Baskaran said the objective was to enable every visually challenged student to write the examinations independently without the help of scribes.

World.title: Paramedical students seek ₹15,000 monthly stipend for hospital training in Andhra Pradesh
World.content:
Paramedical students staged a demonstration at Dr. NTR Health University of Health Sciences (Dr. NTRUHS) on Thursday (September 17, 2026) demanding the immediate resolution of their long-pending issues, including payment of stipends.

Student Federation of India (SFI) State president P. Ramamohan and State secretary K. Prasanna Kumar, who took part in the demonstration, said it was highly unfair that paramedical students, who play an important role in the healthcare sector, do not receive any stipend for their work.

Alleging that the government neglected their welfare, the SFI leaders demanded a minimum monthly stipend of ₹15,000 for providing services in hospitals as part of internships and clinical training.

The SFI leaders raised concerns over delays in completing paramedical courses. Students who enrolled in 2021 are reportedly still awaiting completion, with four-year courses extending beyond six years.

Delays in examinations and the release of results are affecting students’ higher education, employment and competitive examination opportunities, the leaders said.

The SFI urged the government to ensure timely completion of courses, conduct examinations and release results without delay, while also providing stipends.

The students later submitted a memorandum to Dr. NTRUHS Vice-Chancellor P. Chandrasekhar, who assured them that exam-related issues would be addressed and that the other concerns would be taken to the notice of the government.

World.title: Amid Houthi attacks, DG ISPR says Pakistan will 'go to any extent' to defend Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has said that Pakistan will go to “any extent” to defend Saudi Arabia.

He made the remarks in an interview with Arab News, a clip of which was posted on its social media account on X late Wednesday night, which come amid renewed tensions in the Middle East as Yemen’s Houthi rebels carry out attacks in Saudi Arabia.

“Pakistan fully stands with the kingdom of Saudi Arabia, both diplomatically and physically. And I would like to underscore the word physically,” Lt Gen Chaudhry said.

“We will go to any extent for the security of Haramain Sharifain and the kingdom of Saudi Arabia. To any extent as asked and required by our Saudi brothers,” he said.

“It should be clear that the people of Pakistan stand shoulder to shoulder with their Saudi brothers and sisters. There should be no doubt about it,” he said.

“So, in a nutshell, we are there and will continue to defend the kingdom of Saudi Arabia against any aggression,” he said.

The military’s spokesperson added that Pakistan’s politico-military leadership remained in continuous contact and engagement with the Saudi leadership.

He said that at the same time, Pakistan, “very earnestly and sincerely”, was working with the help of regional countries and others to find a “negotiated, peaceful outcome of this complex situation”.

“That’s where the position of Pakistan is,” he said.

In another clip posted on X, he said Pakistan “remained not only committed, but we are already there for the protection of Haramain Sharifain and the kingdom of Saudi Arabia”.

“We are there to protect them,” he asserted, reiterating that Pakistan would “go to any extent” as required by the Saudi leadership.

“Our commitment to Saudi security is unconditional. It stems from a deep-rooted, historical and unbreakable bond between the people of Pakistan and the people of Saudi Arabia, between the political and the military leadership of both countries,” he said.

“So, nothing stops us. Nothing bars us. Nothing is there which hesitates [sic] our commitment. So, whatever is required, whatever is asked, we will go to any extent for that,” he said.

More to follow

World.title: LNG shortages hit Pakistan badly
World.content:
BANGKOK: Pakistan is among the worst-hit nations by liquefied natural gas (LNG) disruptions due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and could future-proof its domestic energy and power supply by increasing its focus on renewables and coal.

“Qatar and the UAE together supply about 99pc of Pakistan’s LNG — mostly for power generation, fertiliser production and industrial use. LNG accounts for about 30pc of total gas supply,” said the Gastech Conferences in its report ‘The Outlook for Gas and LNG Markets in Asia’ released at its 54th annual event.

It said that beyond addressing immediate challenges, policymakers in Asia may now be reviewing how to future-proof domestic energy and power systems with renewed focus on energy security. This could be done by accelerating renewables, such as swift-build, utility-scale solar, wind farms and commercial rooftop solar, plus storage deployment.

They would also be looking at speeding up investment in long-term infrastructure, including gas storage and updating power generation mixes and giving gas plants better flexibility.

Gastech report notes US-Iran war has redrawn global energy maps

This is where Pakistan’s Universal Gas Distribution Company (UGDC) held discussions with several international firms on potential projects, including gas storage, long-term LNG supplies and gas distribution in overseas markets, its Chief Executive Officer Ghiyas Abdullah Paracha said.

The Gastech report said the countries were also examining options for expanding operating reserves to ensure grid agility for unexpected events and rethinking fuel stockpiles by expanding strategic stocks for transport fuels and power generation. The nations may also be looking at boosting cross-border power export/import options to share shortages.

The report said the Middle East’s fluid landscape — as demonstrated by the conflict involving Israel, the United States and Iran which began in February and the resultant bottleneck in the Strait of Hormuz — has redrawn global energy maps in real time and further highlighted the geopolitical sensitivity of gas and LNG markets.

Gastech noted that gas supply disruptions have prompted Pakistan’s government to look to coal, hydropower, and nuclear power, while price volatility and shipping uncertainty are likely to sharply increase power costs.

Ghiyas Paracha told journalists that his company received a greater-than-anticipated response at the conference. “We have got understanding with some companies that have shown interest in building gas storage facilities in Pakistan. Some companies have shown keen interest in long-term LNG contracts with UGDC,” Paracha said.

Paracha said UGDC’s participation at Gastech was also significant because the company was presenting Pakistan’s gas-sector reforms and the opening of the country’s gas market to private-sector participation at an international energy forum.

Published in Dawn, September 18th, 2026

World.title: Govt lowers petrol price by Rs0.43 per litre, raises HSD by Rs3.47 per litre
World.content:
The government on Thursday cut the price of petrol by Rs0.43 per litre but raised that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.47 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs390.79 per litre while HSD will cost Rs424.92 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on Sept 18 (Friday).

According to Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA), the increase is primarily linked to higher petrol and diesel prices in the international market.

The regulator said the prices were revised based on international market rates, premiums and other relevant factors.

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

The government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices, including requiring markets to close by 9pm and cutting fuel allocations for official vehicles by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

A statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said owners of two- and three-wheelers would receive relief of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres, while owners of vehicles up to 800cc would receive the same relief on a monthly quota of 30 litres.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Imaan, Hadi sent on judicial remand in another case after SC suspends sentences
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Hours after the Supreme Court suspended the sentences of human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, an anti-terrorism court (ATC) rejected police’s request for a 30-day physical remand of the couple and sent them to jail on judicial remand.

On January 24, an Islamabad sessions court sentenced Imaan and Hadi to a total of 17 years in jail on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca). The convictions of the couple, who had already been jailed the day before in a separate case, were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts .

Islamabad ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain passed the order after the two accused were produced before the court for a hearing in a case registered against them at Kohsar police station.

Soon after their release, Islamabad police personnel, led by the SSP Operations, reached Adiala jail and arrested the two again in connection with the case. The police subsequently produced them before the ATC late at night.

Former federal minister Shireen Mazari confirmed the development, saying attempts were being made to keep the couple in jail.

Speaking to Dawn, Imaan’s counsel Riasat Ali Azad also confirmed the development, saying a large contingent of Islamabad police had shifted the couple to Kohsar police station.

The case at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station was registered on March 22, 2025, on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio.

Imaan and her husband were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads and were nominated by name in the FIR. However, at the time of registration of the case, no section of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) had been added.

The FIR included Section 188 (disobedience of an order lawfully promulgated by a public servant), Section 341 (wrongful restraint), Section 506 (punishment for criminal intimidation), Section 353 (assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their official duty) and Section 186 (obstructing a public servant in the performance of official duties).

SC suspends sentences
